title: Unacademy, Astrotalk, Noise founders back Triptii Dimri-led startup Peep Beauty in  ₹12 crore pre-seed funding round
content:
Actor Triptii Dimri of Animal fame has joined D2C beauty brand Peep Beauty as one of their co-founders as well as an investor, and has been involved in their creative direction as well as brand storytelling, the company said in a statement on Friday.
The investment made by the actor is a part of the company's pre-seeding funding round of ₹12 crore ($1.2 million), which was led by Sadev Ventures. Other investors like ISV, iSeed, and TDV also participated, as per a report by Inc42.com.
"The association goes beyond a conventional endorsement, establishing a close fit between PEEP Beauty’s identity, its intended consumer and Dimri’s connection with a young and rapidly evolving audience," the company said regarding its association with the actor.
The pre-seed funding round of Peep Beauty also saw participation by some major start-up founders, including Gaurav Khatri of Noise, Roman Saini of Unacademy, Puneet Gupta of Astrotalk, Dhruv Bhasin of Arata, and Arjun Vaidya of V3 Ventures.
Peep Beauty was founded earlier this year by Aman Arora, who was a former co-founder of Keventers. It plans to sell its products through its own platform while increasing its brand visibility across e-commerce and quick-commerce marketplaces.
The company, which launched on 11 September, has a portfolio of coloured contact lenses and liquid eyeshadows, which, as per its press release, is "designed for consumers looking to express themselves through their eyes."
According to Inc42, the company launched its range of eyeshadows to help customers create complete makeup looks that complement their lenses.
The startup claims that it is India's first eye beauty brand.
UBR × DISRPTVE, an integrated venture-building and growth-advisory platform, helped bring the new-age beauty brand to the market.
The platform offers businesses three principal engagement models: fundraising, strategic advisory and end-to-end venture building. It also deploys expertise across capital, talent, design, strategy and distribution based on a brand's stage and requirements.
Dimri's association with this company adds to a long list of celebrities being brought on board by direct-to-consumer brands to increase their visibility.
Earlier this year, Kriti Sanon was brought on as an investor in jewellery brand GIVA, while Shilpa Shetty Kundra joined kids' lifestyle brand Rosada as a strategic investor.
Agilitas Sports, a sportswear brand, brought on Anushka Sharma as an investor while cricketer Ajinkya Rahane was brought on as a strategic advisor as well as investor by footwear brand Chupps.

title: Astrotalk turns unicorn: How astrology became a $1 billion business
content:
Astrotalk turns unicorn: How astrology became a $1 billion business
Astrotalk has entered India's unicorn club through a profit-funded ESOP buyback involving more than 100 employees. The milestone underscores how the company has expanded astrology into a broader spiritual-tech and commerce business.
For a company whose business is built around telling people what the future might hold, Astrotalk has just reached a milestone that is very much about the present: a $1 billion valuation.
The Noida-based astrology and spiritual-tech platform has entered India's unicorn club through an ESOP buyback involving more than 100 employees. The buyback is being funded by profits generated by the company, making the milestone notable not just for its valuation but also for the profitable business it has built.
Founded in 2017 by Puneet Gupta and Anmol Jain, Astrotalk began by connecting users with astrologers. Over the years, it has expanded that proposition into a wider spiritual and wellbeing platform, while continuing to build its core astrology business.
FROM ASTROLOGERS TO A SPIRITUAL-TECH PLATFORM
Astrotalk's website says it now has more than 13,000 astrologers on its platform and facilitates over 1 lakh minutes of consultations every day.
Users can consult astrologers, attend live sessions, get Kundli matching and access daily horoscopes. But the company has increasingly moved beyond the traditional astrology consultation.
Its stated aim has been to retain the ethos of traditional astrology while using spiritual approaches to address modern concerns such as stress and mental wellness.
That has opened up a much wider set of offerings.
The platform now has categories for spiritual jewellery, Rudraksha, Pyrite, Vastu, Dhan Yog and products linked to planets and Mulank. It also has dedicated collections for gifting and spiritual products.
Astrotalk's newer offerings even extend into lifestyle products. Its website currently showcases crystal-infused perfumes, including fragrances positioned around themes such as wealth, confidence and love.
The shift is subtle but significant: astrology is no longer just something users consult Astrotalk for; it is increasingly something they can shop around as well.
THE NUMBERS BEHIND THE ASTROTALK BET
The expansion has come alongside a sharp increase in the company's financial scale.
Astrotalk reported revenue of Rs 1,176 crore and profit before tax of Rs 285 crore in FY25. Its current revenue run rate is more than Rs 2,500 crore, according to the company.
The company says profitability has remained a focus as it has scaled. That is also what has enabled the latest ESOP buyback.
More than 100 employees are getting an opportunity to sell their ESOPs at the $1 billion valuation. The company has not disclosed the total value of the liquidity event.
For employees, the exercise provides a chance to realise some of the value created during Astrotalk's growth. Co-founder Anmol Jain said the buyback reflects the company's focus on building an ownership culture and rewarding employees for their contribution.
FROM HOROSCOPES TO COMMERCE
The bigger story behind Astrotalk's rise is perhaps its ability to build a business around an age-old practice without restricting itself to the traditional way people consume it.
A user may come to the platform looking for an astrologer's advice, but the company has created multiple adjacent categories around spirituality, wellness and commerce.
That gives Astrotalk more opportunities to engage users beyond a single consultation and broadens the business from a service platform into an ecosystem.
Its backers have also placed bets on that growth. Astrotalk is backed by Left Lane Capital and Elev8 Venture Partners. Left Lane invested $20 million in February 2024 and another $14 million in June that year.
The $1 billion valuation comes as Astrotalk prepares for its next phase of expansion.
The company plans to increase its global footprint and invest in technology and talent, while strengthening its position in the spiritual-tech category.

title: How Astrotalk Became a $1 Billion Unicorn Without Raising a New Funding Round
content:
Astrotalk has become India’s latest unicorn but unlike most startups, it did not need a new funding round to get there. The Noida-based online astrology and divination platform reached a $1 billion valuation through an ESOP buyback funded by its own profits, allowing more than 100 employees to sell a portion of their shares while continuing to hold a stake in the company.
The transaction, announced on August 12, 2026, gives Astrotalk unicorn status through an employee liquidity event rather than a fresh infusion of venture capital. The company reported ₹1,176 crore in operating revenue and ₹250 crore in net profit in FY25, while its annualised revenue run rate has now crossed ₹2,500 crore. The growth is driven by its core online consultation marketplace, rapid expansion into spiritual e-commerce via the Astrotalk Store, scaling international markets for the Indian diaspora, and strong user engagement focused on relationships and career advice.
But the more interesting part of the story isn’t simply that Astrotalk has become a unicorn. It is how the company has built a profitable consumer business around a category that was traditionally dominated by offline astrologers, and how that profitability is now giving it an alternative route to growth and employee wealth creation.
How did Astrotalk become a unicorn without raising a new funding round?
Astrotalk’s latest valuation was established through an ESOP buyback rather than a conventional funding round. The company used profits generated by its own business to buy back shares from more than 100 eligible employees, giving them an opportunity to cash out a portion of their holdings while retaining a stake in the company.
Unlike a traditional funding round, where new investors put capital into the company in exchange for equity, the buyback was funded through Astrotalk’s internal accruals. This allows the company to provide employee liquidity without relying on fresh external capital or diluting existing founder and shareholder stakes. It also gives Astrotalk greater flexibility to determine when to conduct a buyback based on its cash flow, while rewarding employees with real liquidity from the value they have helped create.
Astrotalk has not disclosed the total value of the buyback or the amount of shares sold by employees.
What’s Fueling Astrotalk’s Growth?
Astrotalk’s unicorn milestone comes on the back of a business that has grown significantly beyond its core online astrology consultations. The platform has now crossed an annualised revenue run rate of ₹2,500 crore, reflecting the scale of demand it has built around its digital marketplace.
At its core, Astrotalk connects users with astrologers and other spiritual practitioners, with consultations around relationships, careers, marriage and other personal concerns forming a key part of the business.
The company has also expanded into spiritual e-commerce through Astrotalk Store, creating an additional revenue stream beyond consultations. Its international expansion, particularly among the Indian diaspora, is another part of its growth strategy.
Astrotalk has previously raised around $34 million in external funding, including investments from Left Lane Capital, Elev8 Venture Partners and QED Investors. However, the latest employee liquidity event was funded through the company’s own profits.
That shift is significant. After using external capital to build and scale the business, Astrotalk is now generating enough from its operations to create liquidity for employees without depending on another funding round.
So, how does Astrotalk make money?
Astrotalk’s core business is built around an online marketplace connecting users with astrologers, tarot readers and other spiritual practitioners. The platform has onboarded tens of thousands of astrologers, creating a large network of service providers for users seeking consultations around relationships, careers, marriage, finances and other aspects of their lives.
The model effectively takes a traditionally offline service and turns it into a digital marketplace. Users can discover practitioners, choose consultations and pay through the platform, while Astrotalk earns from the transactions.
This marketplace model also gives the company an important advantage; as the number of users and astrologers grows, the platform can create more opportunities for transactions without having to build every service itself.
Astrotalk has also expanded beyond consultations through Astrotalk Store, taking the company further into spiritual and astrology-linked commerce. The business has additionally been expanding internationally, particularly among Indian audiences living outside the country.
Together, these businesses are helping Astrotalk move from being an astrology consultation app to a broader consumer platform built around spirituality and personalised guidance.
From an offline practice to a digital consumer business
Founder and CEO Puneet Gupta built Astrotalk around a simple opportunity ; take a category that already had significant demand offline and make it accessible through a digital platform.
The challenge, however, was trust.
Astrology, Tarot, Vastu are categories where consumers often need confidence in the practitioner before spending money. Astrotalk therefore focused heavily on creating a large network of astrologers, reducing friction for first-time users and investing heavily in digital customer acquisition.
The company used digital advertising, YouTube campaigns and influencer partnerships to bring new users onto the platform.
Over time, the astrologer network became another important part of the platform’s ecosystem. Practitioners aren’t just service providers; their presence creates more choice for consumers and more content and interactions on the platform.
The result is a marketplace where user demand and the supply of astrologers can reinforce each other.
Why the ESOP Buyback Matters
For employees, the buyback creates something startups often struggle to provide: liquidity. ESOPs give employees ownership in a company, but those shares can be difficult to monetise while the business remains privately held. By buying back shares, Astrotalk is giving eligible employees an opportunity to realise part of the value of their equity without requiring the company to go public or bring in a new investor.
For the company and existing shareholders, funding the buyback through internal accruals means Astrotalk can provide this liquidity without a fresh funding round or additional dilution. It also allows the company greater control over when and how it creates liquidity based on its own cash flows, rather than depending on external market conditions or investor timelines.
There is a trade-off, however. Using internal accruals for buybacks could limit the amount of capital available for aggressive expansion compared with competitors backed by large external funding pools. International expansion, acquisitions or other capital-intensive initiatives could eventually require institutional funding, particularly if profitability or cash flows fluctuate.
Still, the transaction signals a degree of financial flexibility. A startup that can fund employee liquidity from its own profits has more control over when and why it raises external capital while reducing its exposure to valuation corrections and difficult market conditions.
What comes next for Astrotalk?
After achieving Unicorn's status, Astrotalk’s ambitions appear to extend well beyond its original online consultation marketplace.The company plans to continue expanding internationally, including in markets such as the United States, while investing in engineering and improving its technology platform.
Its expansion into commerce could also take the business beyond digital consultations and into a broader spiritual consumer category, including offline retail opportunities.That creates a larger opportunity and a larger challenge.
Astrotalk now has to prove that the demand it has built around online astrology can translate into a wider consumer brand across markets, products and formats.
For now, however, its unicorn milestone represents something notable in India’s startup ecosystem. Astrotalk’s story is not simply about becoming a billion-dollar company. It is about building a consumer business that has grown from an offline, trust-driven category into a digital marketplace, reached profitability and now has enough internal cash generation to create liquidity for its employees.

title: Astrotalk turns unicorn at $1 Bn valuation via ESOP buyback
content:
Astrotalk turns unicorn at $1 Bn valuation via ESOP buyback
- ByStartupStory | August 14, 2026
Astrotalk has become a unicorn after reaching a $1 billion valuation through an ESOP buyback, and it is a major milestone for the company. The move shows that the startup has grown enough to cross one of the most closely watched thresholds in the Indian startup ecosystem.
What makes this moment interesting is that the unicorn status came through an ESOP buyback rather than a fresh funding round. That means the valuation reflects confidence in the company’s current strength, while also giving employees a chance to benefit from the value they helped create. In many ways, that makes the milestone feel more grounded and internal than a typical headline-making fundraise.
For Astrotalk, crossing the $1 billion mark is a strong signal that its business has built real scale and market relevance. Companies do not reach this stage by accident. It usually comes after years of product development, customer growth, and steady execution. In a space where trust and repeat use matter, that kind of progress is especially meaningful.
The ESOP buyback also matters from a company culture perspective. It suggests the startup is rewarding employees and recognizing that early team members played a part in the journey. For a fast-growing company, that can help strengthen loyalty and morale, especially when people see a clear link between their work and the company’s success.
This milestone also reflects the broader evolution of the startup ecosystem. A unicorn today is not just a flashy label. It is often a sign that a company has moved from potential into proof. Investors and founders alike tend to watch these moments closely because they indicate that a business has reached a more mature and valuable stage.
For Astrotalk, becoming a unicorn may open the door to even more opportunities. It can improve its brand perception, attract stronger talent, and create more confidence among users and partners. At the same time, it also brings higher expectations. Once a company crosses this line, the market starts asking bigger questions about growth, profitability, and long-term durability.
Overall, this is a significant moment for Astrotalk. Reaching unicorn status through an ESOP buyback makes the milestone feel both financial and human, because it rewards the company’s value while also recognizing the people behind it.

title: Astrotalk Becomes India’s Newest Unicorn After Profit-Funded ESOP Buyback
content:
Noida-based astrology and spiritual-tech platform Astrotalk has entered India’s unicorn club after completing an employee stock option buyback that valued the company at $1 billion, or roughly Rs. 9,500 crore.
The transaction involved more than 100 employees and was funded entirely from profits generated by the business rather than from a fresh external funding round. Astrotalk has not disclosed the total size of the ESOP liquidity programme.
The latest valuation marks a major increase from Astrotalk’s previous funding round. According to reports, the company was valued at around Rs. 2,400 crore in June 2024.
That means its valuation has increased nearly fourfold in about two years, supported by rising revenue and profitability.
Astrotalk reported revenue of Rs. 1,176 crore in FY25 and profit before tax of Rs. 285 crore. The company also said its current annualized revenue run rate has crossed Rs. 2,500 crore.
“Over the years, Astrotalk has focused on building a profitable and sustainable business. The fact that we are able to undertake this ESOP buyback using the profits generated by the company makes this milestone especially rewarding,” co-founder and CEO Puneet Gupta said.

Unlike a typical unicorn funding announcement, Astrotalk’s $1 billion valuation was established through an internal liquidity event rather than a new equity raise.
The ESOP buyback gave employees holding vested stock options an opportunity to convert part of their ownership into cash.
Co-founder Anmol Jain said the programme reflects the company’s focus on creating an ownership culture and rewarding employees for their contribution to its growth.
Astrotalk is backed by Left Lane Capital and Elev8 Venture Partners. Left Lane Capital invested $20 million in the company in February 2024 and followed that with another $14 million investment in June 2024.
Founded in 2017, Astrotalk initially focused on connecting users with astrologers through its online platform. It has since expanded into broader spiritual and commerce-related categories.
Astrotalk now plans to invest further in technology, talent and international expansion as it looks to strengthen its position in the spiritual-tech market.
The unicorn milestone also highlights a different startup growth model. Instead of depending solely on repeated funding rounds, Astrotalk has reached a $1 billion valuation while emphasizing profitability and using internally generated cash to provide employee liquidity.

The reported $1 billion valuation represents a sharp change from AstroTalk’s roughly $300 million valuation reported in 2024.

title: Astrology startup Astrotalk achieves unicorn status at $1 billion valuation via ESOP buyback
content:
Indian astrology and spiritual services platform Astrotalk has reached a valuation of $1 billion through an employee stock option (ESOP) buyback involving more than 100 employees.
The Noida-based startup said the buyback was funded from profits generated by the business, giving eligible employees an opportunity to sell some of their holdings while retaining a stake in the company.
Astrotalk did not disclose the total value of the buyback or how much stock employees were able to sell.
The transaction gives the privately held startup unicorn status, a term used for startups valued at $1 billion or more. The valuation was established through the employee share buyback rather than a fresh funding round.
“This buyback reflects our belief that great companies are built when teams think and act like owners,” co-founder Anmol Jain said.
Founded in 2017 by Puneet Gupta, Astrotalk operates an online marketplace connecting users with astrologers for services including horoscope readings, birth-chart analysis, tarot, numerology and Vastu consultations.
It has since expanded beyond astrology consultations into spiritual products and e-commerce.
Astrotalk said its annualised revenue run rate has crossed Rs 2,500 crore.
Astrotalk recorded operating revenue of Rs 1,176 crore in the financial year ending March 2025 and an adjuster PBT of Rs 285 crore, according to company figures.
The startup is backed by investors including Left Lane Capital and Elev8 Venture Partners.
Its last external financing came in June 2024, when it secured $14 million in a round led by Elev8 Venture Partners, with existing investor Left Lane Capital also participating. The transaction was a combination of primary and secondary investment and valued Astrotalk at about $300 million.
Earlier in 2024, Astrotalk secured $20 million in its first institutional funding round, led by Left Lane Capital.
The $1 billion valuation attached to the latest employee buyback therefore represents a significant increase from the company's valuation at its last external financing.
Astrotalk has also been expanding into spiritual e-commerce through Astrotalk Store.
The startup said the business generated more than Rs 140 crore in revenue in 2025 and processed 1.6 million orders during the year. It has since reached a daily gross merchandise value run rate of about Rs 1 crore, according to Astrotalk.
It has also launched a standalone gemstone platform offering precious and semi-precious stones with laboratory certification, astrology consultations and a replacement policy.
Astrotalk said the platform was intended to address concerns about sourcing and certification in the gemstone market.
Jain said the company had focused on sourcing, merchandising and new product launches over the past year, with the dedicated gemstone platform aimed at building customer trust in the category.
According to Astrotalk, it plans to continue investing in technology and talent while expanding its international presence across spiritual technology and commerce.
It is the eighth Indian startup to reach unicorn status in 2026, following Juspay, Neysa, KreditBee, Skyroot Aerospace, Square Yards, Sarvam AI and Emergent.

title: Can Astrotalk build the Amazon of spiritual commerce?
content:
Can Astrotalk build the Amazon of spiritual commerce?
The astrology startup that built a profitable consultations business is now pushing into ecommerce, gemstones, and offline stores, as it bets on spirituality becoming India's next organised consumer category.
When people think of astrology apps, most picture a narrow product: a consultation call with an astrologer, surrounded by horoscopes and kundli (birth chart) generators.
Astrotalk wants to change this perception significantly.
The Noida-based astrology company, one of India’s largest and most profitable consumer internet businesses, is building a one-stop, full-stack spiritual commerce platform spanning consultations, ecommerce, gemstones, and offline retail.
Over the last three years, the company has quietly transformed from a single-product marketplace into a multi-vertical consumer business operating across India, the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, and Germany.
Its underlying thesis is simple: spirituality in India has always been a large consumer category, but it has remained fragmented, unorganised, and underserved by organised modern retail and technology platforms.
“People usually think astrology platforms stop at consultations,” says Daman Soni, Chief Business Officer - Astrotalk Ecommerce. “But the customer journey naturally extends into remedies, products, gemstones, and eventually offline experiences. We are trying to build that ecosystem.”
The ecommerce bet
While consultation is the core business of Astrotalk, its biggest expansion so far has been ecommerce.
The company launched the Astrotalk Store in November 2024 with an initial investment of Rs 30 lakh. Commercial scaling began in January 2025, and the business generated Rs 140 crore in revenue within its first year of operations, according to Soni.
Astrotalk has since then committed another Rs 40 crore towards expansion of the store and is targeting an annual run rate of Rs 400 crore–500 crore by FY27.
The premise behind the business emerged from a gap that Astrotalk believes existed in Indian ecommerce.
Spiritual products generated significant search demand online, but major marketplaces never built dedicated categories around them. Rudraksh malas were often listed under jewellery, yantras under home décor, and gemstone purchases remained scattered across small sellers and trust-deficient websites.
Soni believes Astrotalk had something those marketplaces lacked: a large, highly engaged user base actively
receiving product recommendations from astrologers during consultations.
“People were already searching for remedies after consultations,” he says. “If we didn’t build that catalogue ourselves, the demand would simply move to fragmented third-party sellers.”
The store currently sells rudraksh malas, yantras, idols, energised bracelets, and region-specific products such as Karungali malas. Certified gemstones are emerging as one of the business’s fastest-growing categories.
Around 90% of sales currently come through Astrotalk’s own website, rather than external marketplaces, suggesting that the consultations business is funneling customers with high intent towards its ecommerce business.
This equation will change over time as the store expands beyond Astrotalk’s existing customer base, says Soni, an ecommerce industry veteran with stint in companies like BoAt and GlobalBees.
He was roped into Astrotalk in 2025 to lead its ecommerce business.
The four verticals
The Astrotalk Store is only one part of the company's broader diversification strategy. In fact, Astrotalk is building across four business lines.
The astrology consultations business acts as a marketplace connecting users with astrologers across six countries. International markets, largely focusing on non-resident Indians, are strategically important for the company because purchase power is significantly higher outside India, improving margins while also creating distribution opportunities for products and remedies.
Consultation has remained the company's profit engine.
The second business line is Astrotalk Store, the ecommerce business, built on top of the consultation engine. The store business currently has a lean team of around 60 employees.
Offline retail is the newest addition. Astrotalk is planning physical stores designed for customers making higher-ticket purchases such as certified gemstones and large idols, where trust and in-person verification remain important. The stores are also expected to target older consumers who are less likely to transact entirely through apps. However, the company is yet to disclose the rollout timeline and the store format.
Gemstones is the fourth and probably the most strategically significant vertical within Astrotalk’s expansion effort.
India’s gemstone market is enormous but deeply fragmented, plagued by counterfeit concerns, inconsistent certification standards, and opaque pricing. Astrological consultations frequently involve gemstone prescriptions worth tens of thousands of rupees. This creates a built-in purchase pipeline from consultation to commerce.
“The gemstone category already exists at massive scale,” says Soni. “The issue historically has been authenticity and trust.”
Astrotalk is attempting to position itself as a trusted retailer in the gemstone market through certified, lab-tested stones and traceable sourcing.
Creating a flywheel
The four verticals together create a significant sales flywheel, one business feeding into the other. Consultations generate demand. Ecommerce captures that demand. Gemstones increase transaction value, while offline retail deepens trust and expands reach beyond digital-native consumers.
Few Indian consumer startups have attempted to build this kind of interconnected business across both digital and physical channels simultaneously.
The logic behind Astrotalk’s expansion is not hard to understand.
Users who trust the platform’s astrologer-verification process are more likely to purchase products recommended during consultations. The consultations business also generates detailed insights into demand signals, the remedies being prescribed, in which regions, and at what frequency—data most ecommerce businesses would otherwise spend heavily to acquire.
The company has already spent nearly eight years proving that digital platforms can aggregate demand for astrology consultations at scale. And its ecommerce business has shown that at least part of this demand can be directed towards products and commerce.
The question now is whether Astrotalk can execute all four verticals simultaneously with the operational quality each requires.
Consultation marketplaces, ecommerce operations, offline retail, and gemstone sourcing involve entirely different supply chains, economics, and management strategies.
Astrotalk reported an operating revenue of Rs 1,176 crore in FY25, growing from Rs 651 crore in FY24.
The company's overall profit declined in FY25, despite revenue more than doubling, reflecting the cost of expanding aggressively across multiple categories at once.
The timing of the expansion adds another layer of challenge. Astrotalk is pursuing expansion while it prepares for a potential IPO, a process that typically absorbs significant management bandwidth and often slows operational decision-making.
The company has set a revenue target of Rs 2,000 crore ahead of its listing, according to Soni. Achieving this target would require both the core consultations business and the store to sustain aggressive growth trajectories over the next 18 months.
Can Astrotalk ultimately evolve into a strong multi-vertical spiritual commerce platform? Or will its consultations business be stretched thin by operational complexity? The outcome depends on how effectively the company manages its next phase of growth.

title: The Ayurveda Co., Khadi Essentials shut down; founder cites rapid expansion, high costs
content:
ADVERTISEMENT
The Ayurveda Co and Khadi Essentials , the direct-to-consumer Ayurveda and wellness brands co-founded by Param Bhargava and Shreedha Singh Bhargava, are shutting down after seven years of operations, with the company having stopped operations in July 2025 and its assets subsequently liquidated.
Bhargava announced the closure in a LinkedIn post on September 3, saying the company is now being formally wound down. The brand has remained inactive since operations were halted last year.
In the post, Bhargava said The Ayurveda Co had generated Rs 250 crore in net revenue and served 20 lakh consumers during its seven-year journey. The company had also built 20 owned stores, 800 business associate counters and more than 10,000 touch points, alongside 110 operational distributors.
The founder said the business had raised Rs 125 crore from venture capital investors and angel investors. He also cited Rs 100 crore in online monthly recurring revenue at its peak and said more than 1,000 people had been associated with the business at one point.
Founded by Bhargava and his wife Shreedha, The Ayurveda Co was built around the objective of making Ayurveda more relevant to younger consumers through a more contemporary and evidence-led approach.
However, Bhargava acknowledged that the company expanded too quickly and across too many areas before its underlying systems were ready to support the scale. He also said the business brought in too many senior employees too early, adding that several decisions would have been made differently with the benefit of hindsight.
Taking responsibility for the outcome, Bhargava said he had repeatedly reviewed the company's decisions in an effort to identify where its trajectory could have changed. He said he remained proud of what the team had built despite the eventual shutdown.
The founder also disclosed the personal financial strain involved in attempting to keep the business afloat, saying he had mortgaged his parental property and gone without a salary for more than a year.
Bhargava apologised to stakeholders who incurred losses and said he personally felt responsible for the money raised and amounts that remain outstanding.
With The Ayurveda Co now being formally closed, Bhargava said he intends to continue building in the health and longevity space. He also indicated that the brand could potentially be available to another entrepreneur interested in building an Ayurveda business.

title: The Ayurveda Co shuts down: founders confirm ₹250 crore venture’s closure after rapid expansion
content:
The Ayurveda Co (TAC), the Ayurveda-focused beauty and personal care brand, is being formally shut down after its operations were stopped in July 2025 and its assets subsequently liquidated, co-founder Param Bhargava said in a LinkedIn post.
Co-founder Shreedha Singh Bhargava also confirmed the closure in a separate LinkedIn post, saying the brand had remained inactive since operations stopped and that the company is now being formally closed.
“I’d rather say this out loud than let it quietly disappear,” she wrote.
The shutdown marks the end of a four-to-five-year run during which TAC scaled to more than ₹150 crore in annual gross merchandise value (GMV), according to Ms. Shreedha. The company had a team of more than 1,000 people across on-roll and off-roll roles and built a significant retail and online presence across India, she said.
Param said that over seven years, TAC and Khadi Essentials, another brand associated with the founders, generated ₹250 crore in net revenue and reached 20 lakh consumers. At their peak, the businesses had 20 owned stores, 800 beauty-adviser counters, more than 10,000 touch points and 110 operational distributors, he said.
Param also said the ventures had raised ₹125 crore from venture capital investors and angel investors.
The founders attributed the eventual failure primarily to the pace and breadth of expansion.
“We expanded too fast, too wide, & way too many senior folks too early, before the system was ready,” Mr. Param said in his LinkedIn post.
Ms. Shreedha similarly wrote: “We expanded too fast, too wide & way too many senior folks too early on, before the system could digest - a small baby had too many mothers.”
The founders said they made significant personal sacrifices while attempting to turn the business around. According to Ms. Shreedha, they mortgaged their parental property and did not withdraw salaries for more than a year.
“Param & I fought very, very hard to keep the boat afloat,” she wrote.
Mr. Param said he took full responsibility for the decisions that did not work and acknowledged that there were several decisions he would make differently.
“I take full responsibility for what did not work, and I am still incredibly proud of what we built together,” he wrote.
The closure also represents a reversal from the founders’ position a year earlier. In a LinkedIn post last year, Mr. Param had said the company was being reshaped around “Functional Ayurveda”, with plans to deepen its presence across Ayurvedic ingestible and topical categories and make Ayurveda more relevant to younger consumers.
In the recent post, Ms. Shreedha said she had repeatedly reviewed the company’s decisions to identify what could have changed its trajectory.
“I’ve post-mortemed every significant & small decision gazillion times over, trying to figure out which one could’ve been the inflection point for a different outcome,” she wrote.
Mr. Param said the closure also affected stakeholders who had backed the business. “...I can only say sorry to all of the stakeholders who also had to bear a few losses because of us,” he wrote.
He said he now wants to build in the broader health and longevity space and indicated that he would be open to discussions with those interested in building in Ayurveda using The Ayurveda Co brand.
Ms. Shreedha said she was “contemplating what my next purpose looks like” as the chapter closes.

title: The Ayurveda Co. Shut Doors With Hard Lessons Learnt for the Founders
content:
The Ayurveda Co. (TAC), the direct-to-consumer ayurvedic beauty and personal care brand that once scaled to more than Rs. 150 crore in annual gross merchandise value, has officially shut down. Co-founder Shreedha Singh Bhargava announced the closure in a candid LinkedIn post, revealing that operations had actually ceased in July last year, with assets since liquidated and the company now undergoing formal winding-up proceedings. Co-founder Param Bhargava confirmed the same on his own LinkedIn post, adding that sister brand Khadi Essentials was closing alongside it.
Founded in 2021 by Shreedha Singh Bhargava and Param Bhargava, TAC set out to make Ayurveda relevant for a younger, “proof-led” generation, building a business that combined online and offline retail across India. The founders had earlier launched Khadi Essentials in 2019. Over its four-to-five-year run, TAC built a team of more than 1,000 people across on-roll and off-roll positions and reportedly raised around Rs. 125 crore in funding, according to Inc42.
From The Highest Point to Closure, Lessons Learnt
“The brand has been inactive since, and I’d rather say this out loud than let it quietly disappear,” Bhargava wrote, explaining her decision to speak publicly rather than let the closure pass unremarked.
In her post, Bhargava reflected on both the scale the company achieved and the toll it took to get there. “It is difficult to reduce all that I feel into one post, but in that 4-5 year sprint with brutally expedited learnings, TAC scaled to Rs. 150+ crore in annual GMV, had a team of 1,000+ people across on/off-roll roles with a significant retail + online presence & reached consumers across India,” she wrote. “But those numbers may not be what I’ll remember most.”
She was unusually direct about the sacrifices she and Param made to try to keep the company running, including mortgaging family property and forgoing salaries. “Param & I fought very, very hard to keep the boat afloat. From mortgaging our parental property to not withdrawing salaries for over a year, I don’t even want to get started on the crazy belief we had that somehow, one day, we’d turn it around,” she wrote, adding that the pressure led to “breakdowns,” which she called “probably both the superpower & the peril of being an entrepreneur.”
What Went Wrong
On what ultimately went wrong, Bhargava pointed squarely at overexpansion and premature senior hiring. “We expanded too fast, too wide & way too many senior folks too early on, before the system could digest – a small baby had too many mothers,” she wrote. “As a founder, you’ll want the absolute best for your brand & everyone associated, but that ambition could sometimes run ahead of what the business can sustainably absorb.”
She said she had gone back over the company’s decisions repeatedly, searching for the point at which things might have gone differently. “I’ve post-mortemed every big & small decision gazillion times over, recorded, made frameworks, mental models, trying to figure out which one could’ve been the inflection point for a different outcome,” she wrote, adding that there were “many” calls she would make differently today, while taking “accountability of what did not work.” She thanked the teams, customers, shareholders, channel partners, mentors and vendors who backed the venture, including some she said she still does not fully understand the loyalty of. As the chapter closes, Bhargava said she is now “contemplating” what her next purpose looks like.
The startup sold through its website, ecommerce marketplaces, exclusive outlets and multibrand stores. Bhargava said TAC owned 20 retail stores, ran more than 800 beauty advisor counters, and had 110 operational distributors, scaling to Rs. 250 crore in net revenue and reaching 20 lakh consumers.
TAC raised a total of $15 million to date from Sixth Sense Ventures, Wipro Consumer Care Ventures, and angel investors including actor Kajal Aggarwal, with its last round, a Rs. 100 crore Series A, closed in 2023.

title: The Ayurveda Co shuts down after raising Rs 125 Cr; co-founder says it expanded too fast
content:
The Ayurveda Co shuts down after raising Rs 125 Cr; co-founder says it expanded too fast
The D2C Ayurveda brand stopped operations in July 2025 and has since liquidated its assets. Co-founder Param Bhargava said the company expanded too quickly and built out its senior team before the business was ready.
D2C beauty and wellness brand The Ayurveda Co (TAC) is formally shutting down, more than a year after it stopped operations, co-founder Param Bhargava said on Thursday. The company ceased operations in July 2025, following which its assets were liquidated.
The brand has remained inactive since then and is now being formally closed. The closure brings the curtains down on a consumer brand that raised around Rs 125 crore in venture capital, built an extensive online and offline distribution network, and at its peak employed more than 1,000 people across on-roll and off-roll roles.
What went wrong
Bhargava attributed the failure largely to expanding faster than the underlying business could sustainably support. He said TAC expanded too quickly across too many channels and hired senior executives before its operational systems were mature enough for that scale. In an effort to turn the business around, the founders went without salaries for over a year and mortgaged family property before ultimately deciding to wind down operations. Bhargava also took responsibility for the strategic missteps, saying there were several decisions he would make differently in hindsight.
Rapid growth and offline expansion
During its run, TAC scaled to more than Rs 150 crore in annual gross merchandise value (GMV), according to Singh Bhargava. Across TAC and the founders' earlier venture, Khadi Essentials, the two businesses generated roughly Rs 250 crore in net revenue and reached 20 lakh consumers over seven years, according to Bhargava. At their peak, the businesses spanned 20 owned stores, 800 beauty-advisor counters, 110 operational distributors, and more than 10,000 retail touchpoints.
Funding and expansion
TAC raised $3 million in 2022 in a round led by Wipro Consumer Care Ventures, with participation from Rahul Gupta of Tricity Technologies and Harsh Gupta of the School of Design and Entrepreneurship. That was followed by a Rs 100 crore ($12.2 million) Series A round in 2023 led by Sixth Sense Ventures, with participation from actor Kajal Aggarwal, startup founders and venture debt funds. The company planned to use the capital to expand its offline presence, strengthen manufacturing and R&D, and build greater digital awareness around Ayurveda.
At the time of the Series A fundraise, TAC had more than 100 products across 20 brand outlets and over 5,000 retail stores. Bhargava had also said then that TAC was aiming to become a profitable unicorn by FY26 and pursue an IPO by FY28. Those ambitions ultimately did not materialise.
What next
Bhargava said he plans to remain in the broader health and longevity space for his next venture. He also indicated that he was open to discussions around The Ayurveda Co brand with entrepreneurs interested in building in the Ayurveda category.

title: The Ayurveda Co Shuts Down After 7 Years Of Expanding Too Fast, Too Wide
content:
D2C ayurvedic beauty brand The Ayurveda Co and sister brand Khadi Essentials have shut down after a seven-year entrepreneurial journey that saw the founders raise Rs 125 crore, build a wide offline and online footprint, and serve millions of consumers.
The closure, announced by co-founder Param Bhargava on LinkedIn, comes more than a year after operations were stopped in July 2025. The companies’ assets have since been liquidated and the entities are now undergoing a formal winding-up process.
The Expansion Trap
Founded by Bhargava and Shreedha Singh, The Ayurveda Co was launched with a stated ambition to make Ayurveda relevant to a younger, proof-led generation. The founders had earlier launched Khadi Essentials in 2019.
The business expanded across skincare, haircare, natural makeup, wellness and supplements, selling through its own website, ecommerce marketplaces, exclusive outlets and multibrand stores.
But the expansion eventually outpaced the company’s ability to support it.
“We expanded too fast, too wide, & way too many senior folks too early, before the system was ready. As a founder, you want the absolute best for your brand & everyone associated with it but sometimes that ambition runs ahead of what the business can sustainably support," Bhargava writes.
A Business Built At Scale
In his post, Bhargava laid out the scale of what the founders had built: “LOST- 7 years of hardwork, 250cr of Net Revenue, 20L Loving consumers, 20 Owned Stores, 800 BA Counters, 10000+ touch points, 110 operational distributors, 100cr Online MRR, 125cr of Venture Capital from Marquee investors & angels, 1000 plus people at once living this dream build TAC.”
The startup had built a significant physical distribution network alongside its digital presence, positioning itself in a competitive and cash-intensive D2C beauty and personal care market.
The Cost Of Staying Afloat
Bhargava said the founders fought to keep the business alive, including by mortgaging their parental property and going without salaries for more than a year.
“We fought very, very hard to keep the boat afloat.”
He also acknowledged the toll of the turnaround effort, “We pushed ourselves way beyond our physical & mental limits, there were breakdowns. That kind of irrational, stubborn belief is probably both the superpower & the peril of being an entrepreneur.”
The post-mortem, he said, has involved revisiting both major and minor decisions that shaped the company’s trajectory.
“I’ve post-mortemed every significant & small decision gazillion times over, trying to figure out which one could've been the inflection point for a different outcome.”
Taking Responsibility
He took responsibility for the outcome while maintaining that the company’s achievements were significant.
“There are many decisions I would make differently today.”
“I take full responsibility for what did not work, and I am still incredibly proud of what we built together. But, it is what it is.”
The shutdown marks the end of a business that raised capital from marquee investors and angels and built a consumer base of around 20 lakh people. Bhargava said the experience had nevertheless left him with the resolve to continue building.
“I GAINED - WISDOM & WILL to still build & achieve my dream of a Billion$ outcome for Myself, my family, my older stakeholders ( in whatever way possible bec i personally feel responsible for every penny i raised and every penny which remains outsanding )& future stake holders.”
As he closes the chapter, Bhargava said his next entrepreneurial ambition would move towards health and longevity.

T.A.C. raised a total of $15 Mn in funding to date from Sixth Sense Ventures, Wipro Consumer Care Venture, and a host of angel investors, including actor Kajal Aggarwal.
The startup last raised ₹100 Cr in its Series A funding round in 2023.
T.A.C’s FY24 revenue grew 67% YoY to ₹59.6 Cr, while loss tripled to ₹68 Cr on the back of expenses that nearly doubled to ₹109.5 Cr.
With the closure, T.A.C has joined a growing list of Indian startups that have shut down operations in 2026. Earlier this week, Savtacart shut shop after failed funding and acquisition discussions. Last month, social networking platform Medial announced its closure after failing to raise fresh funding amid a cash crunch.
Koo cofounder Mayank Bidawatka also shut down his AI-powered photo-sharing startup PicSee after it failed to achieve the scale required to sustain operations. The list also includes quick commerce startup Klydo and online matchmaking platform Juleo.

title: Circle raises ₹25 crore seed funding led by Nexus Venture Partners
content:
- Funding
- 1 min read
Circle raises ₹25 crore seed funding led by Nexus Venture Partners
The company will use the capital to expand beyond Bengaluru, invest in AI-powered pricing, product discovery and verification, and grow its network of Trust Hubs and logistics partners.
Founded in 2025 by Chirag Kataruka and Ankit Misra, Circle operates a managed marketplace for pre-owned goods, combining AI-led technology, human verification, secure payments and logistics. Unlike conventional resellers, the company does not own inventory, allowing buyers and sellers to transact directly through its platform.
“Nearly 40 per cent of our buyers come back within 90 days, and half our sellers list again. That tells us buying and selling pre-owned can become a regular part of people's lives,” said Misra.
Within a year of launch, Circle has facilitated around ₹25 crore in pre-owned sales, attracting more than one million visitors and generating 100,000 listings from Bengaluru, according to the company. Sellers typically find buyers within three days on the platform, compared with the weeks or months that listings can take to sell on classifieds platforms.
Circle's platform spans categories including smartphones, gaming consoles, cameras, office chairs, furniture, watches, handbags and sneakers. It offers product verification and a three-day guarantee, while handling the selling process from listing and pickup to payout.
“India’s pre-owned market is large, but selling used goods remains difficult due to costs, trust & scale. Circle has understood this problem deeply and is executing exceptionally well to solve it. We believe they have the potential to fundamentally reshape how India buys and sells pre-owned goods,” said Suvir Sujan, partner, Nexus Venture Partners.

title: Inner Circle Major hopes take big hit after Sangal loss at Stake Pulse Beat III
content:
Inner Circle were eliminated from Stake Pulse Beat III after losing 0:2 to Sangal in the Group A decider, dealing a major blow to their chances of qualifying for PGL Singapore Major 2026.
The Ukrainian team had been narrowly inside the projected Major invitation cutoff before the defeat. According to the latest HLTV simulation, Inner Circle are now projected outside the qualification range with only a 28.4% chance of reaching Singapore.
INNER CIRCLE LOSE REMATCH AGAINST SANGAL
The result came only hours after Inner Circle had beaten the same opponent 2:0 in their opening match.
They won Anubis 13:9 and Dust2 13:6 in the first series before losing 0:2 to Ninjas in Pyjamas in the winners match, sending them into a rematch against Sangal for a place in the playoffs.
This time Sangal reversed the result.
- Dust2 (pick Inner Circle) — 16:12 in favor of Sangal
Inner Circle led 7:5 at halftime before the teams finished regulation tied at 12:12. Sangal then won all four overtime rounds to steal the map selected by Inner Circle.
- Cache (pick Sangal) — 13:11 in favor of Sangal
Inner Circle again started ahead with a 7:5 first half, but Sangal responded with an 8:4 second half to close the series without requiring Mirage.
Yeray “Joey” Serrano Pérez finished as the highest-rated player in the match with 44–35 K–D, 87.3 ADR and a 1.35 Rating 3.0.
MAJOR QUALIFICATION CHANCES DROP TO 28.4%
The elimination is particularly costly because Inner Circle entered Stake Pulse Beat III as one of the teams fighting around the Major invitation cutoff.
Before the loss to Sangal, the team were projected narrowly inside the qualifying range. The early exit reduced the number of VRS points available to them while several direct competitors remain active in upcoming events.
HLTV now gives Inner Circle a 28.4% projected chance of receiving an invitation to PGL Singapore Major 2026.
The percentage does not mean the team are mathematically eliminated. Their final position will still depend on results from other teams in the qualification race and the rankings at the invitation cutoff.
INNER CIRCLE NOW DEPEND ON RESULTS ELSEWHERE
Stake Pulse Beat III was an important opportunity for Inner Circle to strengthen their position before the Major cutoff, but the group-stage elimination means they can no longer add points through a deeper run at the event.
The team will now have to rely both on their remaining opportunities and unfavorable results for direct competitors around the qualification line.
What began with a 2:0 victory over Sangal ended with elimination against the same opponent, leaving Inner Circle in a significantly more difficult position in the final race for Singapore.

title: Circle Internet Spikes 7% After Backing OKX at $25B Valuation; Coinbase Rallies 6%, Strategy Climbs 3%
content:
Circle Internet Spikes 7% After Backing OKX at $25B Valuation; Coinbase Rallies 6%, Strategy Climbs 3%
Circle Internet just placed a bet on tokenized stock trading by backing crypto exchange OKX, and the ripple across crypto equities reveals which business models investors trust most when the sector heats up.
Circle Internet Group (NYSE:CRCL | CRCL Price Prediction) stock rose 7% to $86.39 after the stablecoin issuer joined a funding round that values cryptocurrency exchange OKX at $25 billion. Crypto-linked equities are rallying alongside it, and the gains in the operating companies are running far ahead of the asset they handle. That spread shows where the buying is focused, with infrastructure names leading and the asset fund lagging.
Meanwhile, Coinbase Global (NASDAQ:COIN) stock is up 6% to $181.91, a gain just behind the advance in Circle Internet stock. Additionally, Strategy (NASDAQ:MSTR) stock is up 3% to $156.40, the lowest advance of the three operating companies yet still well ahead of the benchmark funds.
Measured against two benchmark funds, the crypto equities are running well ahead of both. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (NASDAQ:IBIT) is up 1%, a fraction of the gains posted by all three stocks. The wider market is stronger too, with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) up 0.5%.
OKX Round Pulls Circle Internet Toward Tokenized Trading
Circle Internet joined the latest OKX funding round as a major investor, alongside Ripple and Standard Chartered. OKX is seeking regulatory clearance to trade tokenized stocks, so the investment places Circle Internet closer to a venue where conventional equities and blockchain settlement would meet.
The roster pairs a crypto-native stronger with a global bank, a mix that reflects how closely the two worlds now overlap in tokenization.
Three Business Models Behind One Rally
Circle Internet issues USDC (CRYPTO:USDC), a stablecoin backed by reserves and intended to hold a fixed dollar value. Its income comes primarily from the yield on those reserves. The company gains when the amount of USDC in circulation grows and when interest rates stay high. Cryptocurrency prices play a secondary role in that model, which sets Circle Internet apart from the other two names in the rally.
Coinbase runs an exchange and earns on transactions, so its business gains with trading volume. Strategy makes holding cryptocurrency on its balance sheet the center of its business, which ties it to the asset price more directly than either Circle Internet or Coinbase. Those differences mean each stock answers to a separate set of forces, even when all three rise together.
Circle Internet’s upside argument is that buying into exchange infrastructure turns a single-product issuer into a company with a stake in where tokenized trading settles, a far larger market than stablecoins alone. However, the bear case points out that this is a minority investment in a private company whose central ambition still depends on a regulator’s decision.
What to Watch Next
OKX’s push for clearance to trade tokenized stocks is the open question hanging over the investment. A decision on that clearance is worth monitoring, since much of the strategic value of Circle Internet’s stake rests on it. Approval could strengthen the infrastructure case, while a delay could leave the stake looking like a passive holding.
Whether the operating companies keep outpacing the iShares IBIT fund may indicate how durable the infrastructure thesis is. A narrowing gap could signal that enthusiasm for the operators is fading back toward the asset itself. Given the volatility in this fast-moving sector, Circle Internet stock position sizes should stay measured.

title: OKX Raises New Strategic Funding at $25B Valuation From Circle, Ripple and SC Ventures
content:
Key Takeaways
- OKX completed a strategic investment extension at a $25 billion pre-money valuation with Circle, Ripple, QRT and SC Ventures participating.
- The round extends a March investment led by NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange, which valued OKX at the same $25 billion level.
- OKX says the new capital will support stablecoins, tokenization, institutional markets and broader financial infrastructure rather than only exchange growth.
Crypto exchange OKX has completed a new strategic investment round at a $25 billion pre-money valuation, bringing in Circle, Ripple, Qube Research & Technologies (QRT) and Standard Chartered’s investment arm, SC Ventures.
The October 6 investment extends an earlier round led by Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), in March 2026. OKX did not disclose how much capital was raised in the latest extension.
Unlike a traditional funding round built around financial investors alone, OKX framed the deal around companies that already provide key parts of its infrastructure, including stablecoin issuance, liquidity, payments and custody.
OKX Keeps Its $25 Billion Valuation From March
The latest financing values OKX at the same level as its March round. ICE invested roughly $200 million in OKX earlier this year at a $25 billion valuation.
The new extension did not increase that valuation despite adding several major institutional and crypto investors.
Table 1. OKX Strategic Investment Round
The unchanged valuation means OKX has maintained the price established seven months earlier rather than completing an up-round at a higher figure.
That does not necessarily indicate weaker demand. The participants in the extension are largely strategic partners that already work with OKX across financial infrastructure.
Circle, Ripple, QRT and SC Ventures Join the Round
Each investor brings a different part of the financial stack that OKX says it wants to connect.
Circle is the issuer of the USDC stablecoin, which is integrated across OKX’s platform.
Qube Research & Technologies (QRT) is a global multi-strategy investment manager and institutional counterparty that provides liquidity and risk capacity to OKX.
Ripple contributes payments, liquidity and stablecoin infrastructure. Its RLUSD stablecoin is already available through OKX’s unified order book.
SC Ventures, Standard Chartered’s investment arm, gives OKX another connection to institutional custody and tokenized assets. Standard Chartered acts as custodian for BlackRock’s BUIDL tokenized Treasury fund, which is part of a collateral framework developed with OKX and BlackRock.
OKX Says the Capital Will Support Tokenization and Financial Infrastructure
OKX founder and CEO Star Xu said the company wants to build a platform where users can hold, pay, invest and grow assets within the same financial system.
The funding is expected to support areas including:
- Tokenized real-world assets (RWAs)
- Stablecoin infrastructure
- Payments
- Institutional liquidity
- Custody
- Onchain markets
Xu said the exchange was the company’s starting point, not its final product, and that OKX is increasingly positioning itself as a broader financial technology platform.
The round’s strategic structure also gives OKX closer relationships with companies already operating in those areas, rather than relying only on capital.
The Round Extends OKX’s Partnership With ICE
The latest financing builds directly on OKX’s relationship with Intercontinental Exchange.
ICE invested in OKX in March at the same $25 billion valuation, and the two companies have since expanded their collaboration around tokenized securities.
OKX and ICE have also been developing OKX ICE, a joint venture focused on tokenized US equities, making the October funding round closely connected to OKX’s broader push into TradFi assets rather than simply increasing crypto trading capacity.
Recent OKX Developments
OKX has accelerated its expansion beyond conventional crypto trading during 2026, and one of the most significant areas is tokenized equities.
The company has been working with ICE on infrastructure that could bring US-listed stocks onchain through a regulated structure. We recently covered how OKX and ICE are preparing tokenized stock trading as part of that broader strategy.
OKX has also expanded its institutional and payments products, while working more closely with stablecoin issuers and traditional financial firms.
Why the Flat $25 Billion Valuation Matters
The company did not disclose a higher valuation despite adding Circle, Ripple, QRT and SC Ventures.
The round is therefore best understood as a strategic extension at an unchanged valuation, not a new valuation milestone.
For context, funding announcements can sometimes create the impression that a company has increased in value simply because new investors joined. In this case, the stronger signal is the type of investors involved and the infrastructure relationships they bring.
What Comes Next
OKX is likely to put the new capital toward its tokenization, stablecoin, payments and institutional-market strategy while continuing to develop its partnership with ICE.
Attention will also remain on how quickly its tokenized stock plans progress and whether the company expands the range of institutional collateral and stablecoin products available through the platform.
What this means for you: OKX did not receive a higher valuation in this round, but it added four partners that already support important parts of its infrastructure. The bigger story is not the valuation increase, because there was none. It is OKX’s continued shift from a crypto exchange toward a platform combining stablecoins, tokenized assets, institutional liquidity and custody.

title: OKX Raises New Funding at $25 Billion Valuation From Circle, Ripple, SC Ventures and QRT
content:
Crypto exchange OKX has raised new funding at a $25 billion valuation, bringing in strategic investment from Circle, Ripple, Standard Chartered’s venture arm SC Ventures and quantitative trading firm QRT. The round gives OKX fresh backing from companies operating across several of the most important parts of digital-asset infrastructure, including stablecoins, institutional payments, banking and market liquidity.
The amount of capital raised was not disclosed alongside the $25 billion valuation. Rather than representing a conventional venture round led exclusively by financial investors, the participation of Circle, Ripple and SC Ventures gives the transaction a significant strategic component. Each operates businesses that potentially intersect with OKX as crypto exchanges become increasingly integrated with regulated financial infrastructure. The valuation also places OKX among the world’s most valuable privately held cryptocurrency companies. For OKX, the investment comes as the exchange continues expanding beyond its traditional offshore trading business and seeks regulated access to major financial markets.
Strategic Investors Deepen Institutional Links
Circle’s participation is particularly relevant to OKX’s stablecoin business. Circle issues USDC, one of the world’s largest dollar-backed stablecoins and an important settlement asset across cryptocurrency exchanges, decentralized-finance protocols and institutional blockchain infrastructure. A closer relationship between Circle and OKX could support deeper USDC liquidity and settlement across the exchange’s global products, although the investment itself does not establish any exclusive stablecoin arrangement. Ripple brings a different set of capabilities.
The company has built institutional blockchain payment and custody infrastructure while expanding the ecosystem around XRP and its RLUSD stablecoin. Its participation gives OKX another connection to a major digital-asset company focused on bridging conventional financial institutions with blockchain networks. SC Ventures provides perhaps the clearest link with traditional banking. The unit is the innovation and venture-investment arm of Standard Chartered, which has steadily expanded its involvement in digital assets through custody, trading, tokenization and stablecoin-related initiatives. QRT adds a market-structure dimension through its quantitative trading expertise. Together, the investor group illustrates how cryptocurrency exchanges are increasingly becoming infrastructure partners for financial institutions rather than operating solely as venues for speculative retail trading.
$25 Billion Valuation Raises Stakes for OKX
A $25 billion valuation places substantial expectations on OKX’s ability to grow within increasingly regulated global markets. The company operates one of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges by trading activity and has expanded into institutional services, derivatives, wallets, decentralized applications and payments. Its growth strategy increasingly depends on obtaining regulatory approvals market by market. That represents a broader transformation across the crypto-exchange industry. Platforms that historically served customers internationally through relatively centralized operations are increasingly building locally regulated entities as governments establish dedicated digital-asset regimes. The new investment also provides an important external valuation benchmark for OKX. Private-company valuations do not necessarily correspond directly with public-market capitalization because the terms attached to new shares can vary, and the size and structure of the latest financing have not been disclosed.
The $25 billion figure nevertheless provides a reference point for how the participating investors value OKX’s broader business and future growth potential. The identities of the investors may ultimately prove more important than the capital itself. Circle provides stablecoin infrastructure, Ripple operates blockchain payments and digital-asset services, Standard Chartered connects the company with global banking, and QRT contributes institutional trading expertise. Those relationships could become increasingly valuable as crypto exchanges compete for institutional flows and attempt to connect blockchain markets with conventional finance. The transaction therefore represents more than another private fundraising round.
At a $25 billion valuation, OKX is adding strategic shareholders from several segments of the financial system that crypto exchanges increasingly need to interact with — stablecoin issuers, blockchain payment companies, quantitative trading firms and major global banks. The next measure of the investment’s significance will be whether those shareholder relationships translate into new products, liquidity, distribution or institutional infrastructure as OKX continues its regulated international expansion.

title: Circle, Ripple and Standard Chartered Invest in OKX at $25B Valuation
content:
OKX has closed a new funding round at a $25 billion valuation, drawing investment from stablecoin issuer Circle, payments and blockchain firm Ripple, and Standard Chartered's venture arm SC Ventures, the crypto exchange announced on Tuesday, October 6. A London quantitative hedge fund also joined the round, according to separate reporting, at the same valuation at which the Intercontinental Exchange invested in OKX seven months earlier.
Who Invested and Why It Matters
The composition of the investor group is notable: Circle issues $USDC, one of the largest stablecoins by market capitalization; Ripple operates the XRP Ledger and has its own stablecoin and payments infrastructure; and SC Ventures is the innovation and fintech investment arm of British bank Standard Chartered. Together they represent a cross-section of regulated financial institutions and crypto-native infrastructure builders rather than the venture capital firms that have historically backed crypto exchanges.
OKX framed the round in strategic terms. "Through strategic investment and partnership, OKX is aligning some of the most critical builders of financial infrastructure behind its vision for the next generation of onchain markets," the company said in a statement. CEO and founder Star Xu added: "The exchange was our starting point, and we are evolving into a broader global financial technology platform."

- OKX secured strategic investment from Circle, QRT, Ripple and Standard Chartered’s SC Ventures at a $25 billion pre money valuation, with individual investment amounts undisclosed.
- The transaction extends the funding round led by NYSE parent Intercontinental Exchange in March, which valued OKX at roughly $25 billion.
- All four new investors already work with OKX across key parts of its infrastructure, including USDC and RLUSD stablecoins, institutional liquidity and custody.
- Standard Chartered serves as custodian for BlackRock’s BUIDL within OKX’s institutional collateral framework, while QRT provides liquidity and risk capacity.
- OKX CEO Star Xu said the capital would support the company’s growth and plans to tokenize real world assets as it develops beyond its exchange business.
According to an Oct. 6 announcement from OKX, the latest investment extends the round led by ICE and brings capital from companies already working with the exchange across stablecoins, institutional liquidity, payments and custody. The amount invested by the four companies and their individual stakes were not disclosed.
OKX adds four partners to its $25 billion funding round
Circle, QRT, Ripple and SC Ventures each have an existing commercial or infrastructure relationship with OKX.
Circle issues USDC, which is used across the exchange’s trading products. QRT serves as an institutional counterparty and provides liquidity and risk capacity, while Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin is available through OKX’s unified order book.
Standard Chartered already handles part of the exchange’s institutional custody infrastructure. Its venture arm, SC Ventures, is participating in the investment.
OKX founder and CEO Star Xu said the company intends to build a financial technology platform spanning holding, payments and investing while using crypto infrastructure alongside standards used by global financial institutions.
“The exchange was our starting point, and we are evolving into a broader global financial technology platform,” Xu said.
Capital from the round will support the company’s continued growth and plans to tokenize real world assets, according to Xu. OKX did not provide a breakdown of how much of the new funding would be allocated to individual products or markets.
The four investors join ICE, which made a strategic investment in March. As crypto.news previously reported, the deal valued OKX at $25 billion and gave the NYSE parent board representation.
ICE and OKX paired the investment with plans to work together on regulated market infrastructure. OKX would provide spot crypto pricing that ICE could use for regulated U.S. futures products, while the exchange planned to give its users access to ICE futures and tokenized NYSE equities, subject to regulatory approval.
Their relationship has since moved into additional markets. In May, the companies agreed to use ICE Brent and WTI benchmarks for oil perpetual futures offered by OKX in selected jurisdictions.
Circle investment follows deeper USDC integration on OKX
Circle’s equity investment follows several months of work to put USDC across more parts of OKX’s trading and blockchain infrastructure.
In September, Circle and OKX expanded USDC trading across spot, margin and futures markets. Eligible users gained more access to USDC denominated markets, while OKX introduced a USDC Margin Growth Program funded by Circle.
Their existing relationship had already covered dollar to USDC conversions and support for the stablecoin on X Layer, the Ethereum compatible layer 2 network developed by OKX.
A month earlier, Circle deployed native USDC on X Layer together with its Cross Chain Transfer Protocol. The setup lets applications use Circle issued USDC directly instead of relying only on bridged versions of the stablecoin.
Circle co founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire tied the investment to the companies’ existing work.
“USDC’s integration across OKX’s platform demonstrates what it looks like when regulated dollar infrastructure meets one of the world’s most active onchain trading environments,” Allaire said.
Circle has been building similar connections with financial institutions outside OKX. Its Arc blockchain went live on public mainnet in September with institutional validators including BlackRock, DTCC, Visa, Mastercard and Standard Chartered. The network uses USDC for gas and launched with tokenized funds among the assets supported from the start.
Standard Chartered already handles OKX institutional collateral
Standard Chartered’s role reaches into custody and collateral used by institutional traders on OKX.
In April, OKX added BlackRock’s BUIDL tokenized U.S. Treasury fund to its institutional collateral framework with the bank. Eligible institutional and VIP clients can use BUIDL as trading margin while keeping the asset off exchange with Standard Chartered.
Under the arrangement, OKX handles margining and liquidation through its trading system, while Standard Chartered holds the collateral separately. Clients retain ownership of BUIDL and its yield.
The BUIDL setup built on a collateral mirroring relationship between the two companies that began in 2025. Institutional customers can keep eligible assets with the bank while their value is mirrored into an OKX trading account, reducing the need to move the underlying collateral onto the exchange.
Alex Manson, CEO of SC Ventures, said institutional participation in digital assets requires infrastructure that includes institutional grade custody.
“Our partnership with OKX reflects the importance of such infrastructure in enabling the onchain economy,” Manson said.
Standard Chartered has separately worked with Circle to give eligible institutional clients access to USDC minting and redemption through its banking platform. The bank led USDC service launched through its operations in the Dubai International Financial Centre, with possible expansion to other markets subject to approvals.
Ripple and QRT bring stablecoin and liquidity ties
Ripple enters the investor group with RLUSD already integrated into OKX’s trading infrastructure.
The stablecoin operates through the exchange’s unified order book, while Ripple works across payments and liquidity infrastructure. Jack McDonald, Ripple’s senior vice president of stablecoins, said the investment could lead to more work between the companies across stablecoins, payments and institutional markets.
“Stablecoins are becoming a core part of global financial infrastructure, and scaled platforms like OKX will play an important role in driving that shift,” McDonald said.
QRT approaches the relationship from the institutional trading side. The global multi strategy investment manager is a major counterparty to OKX and works with the exchange on liquidity, risk capacity and the rollout of new products and markets.
Thomas Eaton, quantitative trading director at QRT, said its investment was based on the firm’s confidence in OKX and the long term growth of digital assets and round the clock markets.
The latest funding leaves the size of each investment undisclosed. OKX described the transaction as an extension of the ICE led round and maintained the same $25 billion pre money valuation announced for the new investment.
