title: Centroid reopens TaylorMade sale as F&F extends financing, bidders circle
content:
This article was displayed on the ChosunBiz MoneyMove (MM) site at 5:24 p.m. on Apr. 27, 2026.
Centroid Investment Partners (hereinafter Centroid), which is pushing to sell global golf brand TaylorMade, plans to redo the preliminary bidding soon.
As U.S. Old Tom Capital, which had been selected as the preferred negotiating partner, failed to raise funds within the deadline, Centroid plans to open the door to other candidates, including bidders that had earlier expressed interest in the acquisition. F&F, which holds the right of first refusal, is also signaling its intention to acquire by extending by half a year the letter of commitment (LOC) for acquisition financing it received from Samsung Securities and others.
According to the investment banking (IB) industry on the 27th, JPMorgan and Jefferies, the sell-side advisors for the TaylorMade sale, decided to hold another preliminary bid and are communicating in advance with four to five potential bidders. Some have said the preliminary bid will be completed in May and the main bid will be held at the end of June, but it appears no specific schedule has been set.
JPMorgan and Jefferies had previously selected Old Tom Capital, founded by Evan Roosevelt of the Roosevelt family, as the preferred negotiating partner through the main bid for the TaylorMade sale in November last year. Old Tom Capital submitted a price of more than $3 billion (about 4.43 trillion won) and conducted due diligence, but it is said to have failed to complete fundraising within the exclusive preferred period that had been scheduled for last month.
F&F, which holds the right of first refusal, is also said to remain strongly intent on the acquisition. F&F had previously received letters of commitment (LOCs) for 4 trillion won in acquisition financing and bridge loans from Samsung Securities, Mirae Asset Securities and Korea Investment & Securities Co., and it has been confirmed that this deadline was extended by six months. (Related article☞[Exclusive] F&F eyeing right of first refusal for TaylorMade teams up with Mirae, Samsung and Korea Investment & Securities Co.)
It has reloaded its dry powder on the view that a preferred negotiating partner will be selected within six months. The structure reportedly provides part as acquisition financing and the remainder as an ultra-short-term bridge loan until the proceeds from F&F's sale of its TaylorMade equity are deposited.
The market sees a strong possibility that the TaylorMade sale price will be set in the 4 trillion won range. Despite a slowdown in the global golf market, TaylorMade is said to have posted solid results last year.
The key to the TaylorMade sale is price expectations. The industry estimates TaylorMade's EBITDA last year at more than $200 million (about 300 billion won). Considering that the 2025 results-based EV/EBITDA for Acushnet, the parent of Titleist and FootJoy, is around 16 times, TaylorMade's theoretical enterprise value could rise to the high-4 trillion won range. If we consider that Callaway's 2025 results-based EV/EBITDA is around 12 times, TaylorMade's expected sale price could fall to the mid-to-high 3 trillion won range, but Callaway faces a valuation discount factor as it is being reshaped into a pure golf equipment company after the separation sale of Topgolf.
An IB industry official said, "Since a price above $3 billion was confirmed in the bidding process at the end of last year, there is no incentive for the seller to lower the price," adding, "This time, what matters more than price is which candidate can definitely close the transaction."

title: Raising money on Funding Circle: A small business guide
content:
Raising money on Funding Circle: A small business guide
Funding Circle connects businesses with investors looking to lend to British companies, enabling a business loan potentially in a matter of days.
The platform only does business lending, and offers a quick application process, dedicated account manager and a fast decision at the end of the process.
Companies can apply any time online, and Funding Circle says you’ll get a decision typically in 24 hours. Once accepted, the money will be in your account in a few days.
Through the platform, you can borrow up to £350,000 unsecured with a personal guarantee. Rates start at 4.9 per cent and there are no early repayment fees.
Businesses get a dedicated account manager to guide you on every step, so you can stay focused on your business.
Funding Circle says it has helped over 24,000 UK businesses borrow over £2.4 billion, and that 94 per cent of customers would come back to them first in the future.
Who can apply for a business loan?
Limited companies, limited liability partnerships (LLPs) and non-limited companies that have at least two years of filed or formally prepared accounts can apply. For non-limited companies Funding Circle would typically need to see a minimum annual turnover of £45,000 in a company’s latest accounts. The site allows visitors to check if they’re eligible for a business loan online in just 30 seconds.
Types of business loans
Unsecured loans up to £350,000: These are highly flexible loans that can be used for a wide range of purposes, including working capital, expansion capital, asset purchase and more.
Secured loans up to £1 million: These loans can be used for a wide range of purposes and will allow you to borrow more for your business.
A personal guarantee from the majority shareholder(s) is required for all of the above.
What Funding Circle looks for
The credit assessment team use the information you provide, as well as information from credit bureaus and other third parties.
Once you’ve checked your business is eligible, you’ll need to complete the short online application and provide the following supporting documents:
- Most recent filed/formally prepared accounts
- Last three months of business bank statements
These can be uploaded online or emailed across. The platform may also request management accounts, depending on the age of your most recently filed/formally prepared accounts, and other supporting documents if necessary.
How long does the process take?
The application form only takes 5-10 minutes to complete. Then, the Funding Circle credit assessment team will assess your application, making a decision typically within 24 hours. Once you’re accepted, the funds will be in your account in a few days.
What interest rate will your business pay back?
When Funding Circle makes you an offer, you’ll be given an interest rate based on its assessment and the amount of time you want to borrow for. They start at 4.9 per cent per year and are fixed for the duration of your loan, so you know exactly what you’ll be paying each month.
What fees are charged?
With Funding Circle there is only one fee, which is paid when you take out your loan. There are also no early repayment fees, so you can settle your loan early with no extra cost. You’ll only pay interest on the time you borrowed the money, so if you pay back early, you pay less.
The fee varies from between 1.5 and 6 per cent. The fee amount will depend on the credit assessment and the loan term you have requested.
How are the repayments structured?
You’ll need to pay your loan back in equal monthly instalments over your chosen time period.
Make sure you get your ID documents to us to set up a direct debit as soon as you can, as your first repayment is due one calendar month after your loan request closes. This is to ensure payments are on time for the investors who have lent to you.
Who’s lending to me?
With more than 60,000 investors, including thousands of people, local councils, universities and the government-backed British Business Bank, the platform gives all types of investors, big and small, the chance to lend to British businesses.
Your loan may be funded by lots of investors lending small amounts, or by one large investor.
Can I apply for a second loan?
Many find it’s easy to apply for another loan, as you’ve been through the process once before. You’ll typically need to have made at least three to six months of repayments on your existing loan before applying. Businesses with great repayment records can apply for further finance earlier.
You can check if you qualify for a business loan online in just 30 seconds or call 0800 848 8747.

title: Cradlewise Raises $12 Mn In Series A Funding Led By 3One4 Capital
content:
Cradlewise, a child sleep and wellness technology company, has raised USD 12 million in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital, according to a media report. Prudent Investment Management and other investors also participated in the round.
The company, founded by Radhika Patil and Bharath Patil, develops a smart crib that combines a crib, contactless monitoring, motion-based soothing and a connected application. Its system is designed to identify early signs of stirring and activate a gentle bouncing motion before the child fully wakes up.
The startup said the device uses sensors to track sound, movement and posture-related cues. Its software processes these inputs in real time to predict wakefulness and initiate motion-based soothing. The product also receives over-the-air software updates.
Cradlewise plans to use the funding for product research and development, channel expansion, geographical growth and its product roadmap beyond the smart crib. The company said it intends to develop software-led sleep routines, related child-sleep hardware and reusable sensing modules for older children.
The company operates an in-house manufacturing facility in Pune, which it uses for the assembly of its smart cribs. It said the facility enables oversight of manufacturing, material sourcing, product safety and structural testing while supporting its expansion plans.
Radhika Patil leads the company’s strategy, product vision, go-to-market operations and partnerships. Bharath Patil oversees hardware, embedded systems, sensing technology, artificial intelligence and product engineering.
The company said its product is aimed at reducing the need for parents to use multiple separate nursery products, such as bassinets, cribs, white-noise machines and video monitors.
A spokesperson for 3one4 Capital said the investment was based on Cradlewise’s product technology and its manufacturing model.

title: Cradlewise raises $12 million Series A led by Prudent Investment Management, 3one4 Capital
content:
Cradlewise raises $12 million Series A led by Prudent Investment Management, 3one4 Capital
- Published OnSep 4, 2026 | 16:38 IST
- Last Updated OnSep 4, 2026 | 16:38 IST
Cradlewise, an AI-focused consumer tech company, raised $12 million in Series A funding led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management, totaling $26 million.
Cradlewise Inc., an AI-focused consumer technology company developing products for infant and child sleep, has raised $12 million in Series A funding led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management.
The company said it will use the funding for product research and development, expansion of distribution channels and international growth.
Founded in 2019 by Radhika Patil and Bharath Patil, Cradlewise develops smart cribs that use sensors and software to detect signs of a baby's movement and sleep patterns and respond with automated soothing. The company is headquartered in San Francisco and has manufacturing operations in Pune.
The latest funding takes Cradlewise's total capital raised to $26 million. Earlier investors include Sean O'Sullivan Ventures, Footwork VC and Charles River Ventures, along with 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management.
Cradlewise said it plans to expand through online and retail channels, partnerships and international markets. It also plans to develop additional products and software focused on child sleep, including offerings beyond its current crib product.
"We are excited to partner with Radhika and Bharath as they scale into the next phase of growth," said Anand Batra, Investments Team, 3one4 Capital.
"Cradlewise sits at the intersection of two themes we've been tracking closely—AI-native consumer hardware and the shift from passive monitoring to active, intelligent intervention," said Prashasta Seth, Managing Partner and Chief Executive Officer, Prudent Investment Managers.
Radix Capital Advisors, led by Abhishek Taparia, was the investment banking advisor to Cradlewise for the funding round.

title: Cradlewise raises $12 million to make AI cribs for newborns: What about DPDP compliance?
content:
Consumer health and wellness startup Cradlewise, which makes AI-powered cribs for toddlers, has raised $12 million (~Rs 113 crore) in its Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management.
The company plans to deploy the fresh capital towards growth initiatives, research and development (R&D), new sales channels and international expansion.
Founded in 2017 by husband-and-wife duo Radhika Patil and Bharath Patil, Cradlewise describes itself as an AI-first consumer tech company that makes smart cribs designed to soothe babies and help improve family sleep.
The company’s AI-enabled cribs use sensors to track a babyâs movements, sounds, sleep patterns and other contextual signals. Its system uses this data to predict when a baby is likely to wake up and intervene before the baby fully wakes up.
Cradlewise says its technology has learnt from more than 75 hours of infant sleep. Its Pune facility can reportedly produce thousands of AI cribs each month. The company claims that its product can save parents as much as two hours of effort every day.
The platform competes against the likes of SNOO, Elvie Rise and 4moms MamaRoo Sleep, among others.
What’s next for the company? Over the next phase, Cradlewise intends to expand access through a broader set of online, retail, partnership, and international channels.
The next set of initiatives will take the company beyond the crib with software-led sleep routines, related child sleep hardware, lower-priced entry points, and reusable sensing and electronics modules that can shorten future product development cycles.
The roadmap is designed to extend relevance from the 0-24 month infant window into later childhood.
Commenting on the fundraise, Anand Batra, Investments Team, 3one4 Capital said, “Cradlewise is solving an acute parenting problem with a rare combination of product depth, data, manufacturing control, and customer trust. Radhika and Bharath have built a differentiated sleep system with strong unit economics and a roadmap that can extend the customer relationship beyond infancy.”
What remains unclear: Cradlewise has disclosed neither the valuation at which new investors joined the cap table nor the share of equity surrendered to them.
- Moreover, it has not shared its current revenue, profit or losses, gross margin, customer acquisition cost, expenses, number of cribs sold or subscription data.
- In May 2025, Cradlewise moved away from a one-time pricing model and introduced subscription plans for new buyers. Its rationale was rather odd. The company cited new tariffs and rising costs, saying they were making it challenging to deliver the product while maintaining quality and innovation.
- The public funding trail also leaves some questions open. Cradlewise says it has now raised $26 million. Its website says it raised $1 million in 2019 and $7 million in 2021. Adding the latest $12 million takes the visible total to $20 million.
What kind of child data Cradlewise collects for its AI cribs? Cradlewiseâs privacy policy states that the platform can collect a babyâs name, profile image, date of birth and gender.Â
- The company can also collect a babyâs sensory and health data, which includes images, event-based video clips without audio, audio spectrograms, movement, breathing rate, prematurity status, sleep patterns, physical measurements and crib-usage data.
- A parent can turn off data uploads. However, the policy says that when data uploads have not been disabled, periodic images, sampled video clips, audio spectrograms and sensory information can be used for the purposes of training the AI for Smart Smoothing.
- As an Indian user, parents automatically consent to the collection, transfer, storage and processing of their personal data in the US.
âWe do not knowingly collect personal information directly from children under 13. If we learn that a child has provided personal information to us directly, without parental consent, we will delete that information and close any associated account as required by applicable law, including the Childrenâs Online Privacy Protection Act,â says Cradlewise.
Does this sit with Indiaâs data protection law? “The Cradlewise device and services may collect video, audio, movement, sleep, and related sensor data about a child solely because a parent or legal guardian chooses to enable these features for their household,” the company’s privacy policy says.
While Cradlewise is not sinister, Indiaâs Digital Personal Data Protection Rules (DPDP Rules, 2025) prohibit behavioural monitoring of children.
- Section 9(3) of the DPDP Act says, âA Data Fiduciary shall not undertake tracking or behavioural monitoring of children or targeted advertising directed at children.â Parental consent cannot override this restriction.
- Technically, infant sleep data â including physical movement, sleep patterns, etc. â is behavioral data.
Investors take a shine to deeptech: The fresh investment in Cradlewise comes at a time when Indian deeptech startups are attracting large cheques from investors. Earlier this week, smart ring maker Ultrahuman raised $60 million in its Series C funding round led by Qualcomm Ventures. Temple founder Deepinder Goyal also participated in the round.
In June, Sarvam raised $234 million in its Series B funding round at a $1.5 billion valuation. Of the total, $150 million came from HCLTech, the IT subsidiary of Indian conglomerate HCL Group. Bessemer Venture Partners also participated alongside existing backers Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners.

The startup has developed AI enabled cribs that combine sensing, learning, and soothing functions in what it describes as a closed loop system, using data on a baby's movement, sound, and sleep state to try to predict and intervene before the baby fully wakes up. According to Cradlewise, its technology is backed by patents covering its hardware and sensing systems, and the startup claims it has collected over 75 million hours of sleep data that it uses to continuously improve detection, prediction, and personalisation. "Cradlewise came from our own experience of sleepless nights as parents. We wanted to build something that does more than just inform parents that the baby is awake. And more importantly, we take pride in building the engine that fuels this innovation out of India."

title: Cradlewise Raises $12 Million in Series A Round Led by 3one4 Capital, Prudent Investment
content:
Consumer health and wellness company Cradlewise has raised $12 million in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management. The latest investment takes the company’s total funding raised to date to $26 million.
Cradlewise has previously received backing from Sean O’Sullivan Ventures, Footwork VC, Charles River Ventures, 3one4 Capital, and Prudent Investment Management.
The company plans to use the new capital to support business growth, expand its distribution channels, invest in product research and development, and enter new geographic markets.
Smart cribs built around infant sleep
Founded in 2019 by Radhika Patil and Bharath Patil, Cradlewise is an AI-first consumer technology company focused on infant sleep. Its flagship products are smart cribs designed to soothe babies while helping families get better sleep.
The company’s technology combines hardware, sensors, artificial intelligence, and a connected app to monitor a baby’s sleep environment and detect early signs of movement or stirring.
Its smart cribs use sensors to track factors including movement, sound, sleep state, and other contextual signals. The system then processes this information to predict when a baby may wake up and respond before the child fully wakes.
This approach is designed to reduce interruptions during sleep and help parents spend less time manually settling their babies.
AI and sleep data drive the technology
Cradlewise says its technology can save parents up to two hours of effort each day. The company has also developed patents covering its hardware and sensing systems.
According to the company, its AI models have been trained using more than 75 million hours of sleep data. This data forms a key part of the system’s ability to identify patterns associated with infant movement and sleep.
The company’s smart sleep system combines a crib, contactless monitoring, adaptive motion, and a connected application. Together, these features are designed to identify early signs that a baby is beginning to stir and help settle the baby before a complete wake-up.
Pune facility supports manufacturing control
Cradlewise also operates an integrated manufacturing facility in Pune. The facility handles production, testing, and packaging, with the capacity to produce thousands of cribs each month.
Having manufacturing operations under its own control allows the company to manage different stages of production while maintaining oversight of quality and product development. Cradlewise also says the setup gives it greater control over costs.
The manufacturing infrastructure is expected to support the company as it expands its channels and reaches more customers across different markets.
Funding to support wider expansion
The latest Series A round comes as Cradlewise continues to build its position at the intersection of consumer technology, artificial intelligence, and parenting.
Its products are focused on one of the recurring challenges faced by families with infants, particularly disrupted sleep and the resulting fatigue experienced by parents.
With the new $12 million investment, Cradlewise is set to focus on expanding its reach, strengthening its product development efforts, and entering additional geographic markets. The funding also gives the company further resources to develop its technology and broaden the availability of its smart sleep solutions.

title: Cradlewise’s AI Crib Puts Babies to Sleep. Its $12-Million Funding Leaves the Numbers Wide Awake
content:
Cradlewise’s AI Crib Puts Babies to Sleep. Its $12-Million Funding Leaves the Numbers Wide Awake
The baby stirs. A camera detects movement. Sensors register sounds and the opening of the child’s eyes. The crib concludes that a full awakening may be approaching. Before a whimper becomes a cry, it begins to bounce.
The baby may return to sleep. The parents may never know that a small domestic crisis has been detected, interpreted and resolved without them.
This is the promise of Cradlewise, the artificial intelligence-powered crib created by wife-and-husband founders Radhika and Bharath Patil. It is a bassinet, crib, baby monitor, sound machine and automated soothing system compressed into one expensive piece of nursery furniture.
Investors appear ready to lose sleep over it.
Cradlewise has raised $12 million in a Series A round led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management. The company plans to spend the money on growth, research and development, new sales channels and international expansion.
Zeroing In on ECI
09 Oct 2026 - Vol 05 | Issue 41
Constitutional legitimacy versus political opportunism
The announcement arrives wrapped in impressive numbers. Cradlewise says its technology has learnt from more than 75 million hours of infant sleep. Its Pune facility can reportedly produce thousands of cribs each month. The company also claims that its product can save parents as much as two hours of effort every day.
Yet the numbers that describe the business remain tucked firmly under the blanket. Cradlewise has disclosed neither the valuation at which the new investors entered nor the equity surrendered to them. It has offered no current revenue, losses, gross margin, customer-acquisition cost, cash burn, number of cribs sold or subscription-conversion rate.
The crib knows when the baby is about to wake. The funding announcement does not reveal whether the company’s economics have awakened.
A ₹1.6-Lakh Lullaby
Cradlewise began with a problem familiar to almost every new parent: exhaustion.
The Patils built an early version for their daughter in 2017. The company raised $1 million in 2019, conducted a San Francisco pilot in 2020 and secured a $7-million seed round in 2021. It began shipping across America in 2022 before bringing the product to India.
The crib is proudly made in India. It is also priced for a sliver of India.
Cradlewise’s Indian website lists an MRP of ₹1,99,900 and a selling price of ₹1,59,900. In America, depending on the delivery schedule, it costs between $1,499 and $1,799.
For that price, parents receive a crib that can serve a child from birth to 24 months. Its built-in camera and sensors watch for early signs of waking. The machine then uses motion and sound in an attempt to soothe the child back to sleep. Parents can view the baby remotely, monitor sleeping patterns and personalise the crib through an app.
The appeal is deeply human. Sleep deprivation can turn an otherwise joyous period into a nightly endurance test. Wealthy parents already spend heavily on night nurses, sleep consultants, premium monitors and devices that promise a few additional hours of rest. Cradlewise has placed all those anxieties inside a single product.
“At ₹1.6 lakh, Cradlewise is not selling a crib. It is selling exhausted parents the possibility of sleep,” says Ashita Aggarwal, professor of marketing at SP Jain Institute of Management & Research. That can create a powerful premium brand, but the company must prove that demand extends beyond affluent early adopters.
That is the first great test for the fresh capital.
A premium price can support attractive margins if customers willingly pay for a differentiated product. It can also conceal a shallow addressable market. Cradlewise says thousands of families use its cribs, but it has not disclosed sales volumes by geography, factory utilisation or the percentage of buyers arriving through expensive online advertising, retailers and referral programmes.
The company now wants to widen distribution, enter more markets and develop additional products. Global scale, however, requires far more than adding countries to a shipping menu. Baby products carry onerous safety obligations, hardware requires working capital and international logistics can consume the margin created by manufacturing in India.
Then there is the awkward fact that babies grow.
Cradlewise may last two years. A software customer can last decades. That helps explain why the company has already started building a business that continues after the crib has been purchased.
The Crib Sleeps. The Business Subscribes
In May 2025, Cradlewise moved away from a purely one-time pricing model and introduced subscription plans for new buyers.
Its explanation was unusually revealing. The company cited new tariffs and rising costs, saying they were making it harder to deliver the product while maintaining quality and innovation.
That shift matters when asking why $12 million is arriving now.
Every new crib includes two years of the Nurture Core plan. It provides smart soothing, access for multiple devices, personalised soundtracks and 14 days of sleep history. When the two-year period ends, parents using the same crib for another child must pay $9.99 a month to retain Core. The machine continues to bounce and soothe without payment, although the free tier sharply reduces data history and other features.
Nurture Plus goes further. It offers complete sleep history, video summaries, additional caregivers, video alerts, browser streaming, Spotify integration and the ability to record a parent’s voice for personalised lullabies.
Even twins require separate plans.
A product that was sold as an intelligent crib is gradually acquiring the economics of connected software. The hardware brings the camera and sensors into the nursery. The app keeps the family inside the ecosystem. The subscription creates revenue that can recur long after the manufacturing and delivery costs have been incurred.
That model can dramatically improve the business. It can also produce resentment when customers paying nearly ₹1.6 lakh discover that some of the most useful data and video features live behind another payment.
Cradlewise has not disclosed how many customers subscribe, which plan they select, how many cancel or how much software contributes to revenue. Those numbers would reveal whether Nurture is a meaningful recurring business or simply an attempt to protect hardware margins from tariffs, cloud-storage expenses and rising costs.
A $12-million Series A is substantial for a consumer-hardware startup. “Yet the announcement discloses no valuation, revenue, cash burn, gross margin or dilution. Investors may know the economics. The market does not,” says Aggarwal.
The public funding trail also requires clarification. Cradlewise says it has now raised $26 million. Its own published journey identifies $1 million in 2019 and $7 million in 2021. Adding the latest $12 million takes the visible total to $20 million.
The remaining $6 million may have arrived through smaller equity tranches, debt or instruments that were never publicly announced. There is nothing inherently troubling about that. But a funding announcement celebrating the cumulative total should make its composition easy to understand, particularly when databases previously identified a debt round.
Investors will have examined the cap table. Readers have been given a bedtime story.
Seventy-Five Million Hours of Baby Data
Cradlewise’s most formidable asset may eventually be neither the crib nor the Pune factory. It may be the extraordinary quantity of intimate data generated in bedrooms every night.
The company says more than 75 million hours of sleep data improve the system’s ability to detect, predict and personalise its responses. Each additional baby potentially teaches the model more about movements, sounds, sleep states and the moments preceding a wake-up.
This is how the product may create a genuine technological moat. A rival can manufacture a bouncing crib. Replicating years of labelled infant-sleep data is harder.
The sensitivity of that information makes trust equally important.
Cradlewise’s privacy policy says the platform can collect a baby’s name, photograph, date of birth and gender. Its sensory and health information can include images, event-based video clips without audio, audio spectrograms, movement, breathing rate, prematurity status, sleep patterns, physical measurements and crib-usage data.
The policy says that when data uploads have not been disabled, periodic images, sampled video clips, audio spectrograms and sensor information may be used to train the artificial intelligence powering Smart Soothing. Indian users also consent to their personal data being transferred to and processed in the United States.
Parents can disable data uploads. Cradlewise says it employs reasonable safeguards and uses children’s information to operate and improve the service. It also acknowledges a reality that applies to every connected device: absolute security cannot be guaranteed.
Seventy-five million hours of sleep data could become a formidable technological moat. But infant data carries an exceptional burden of trust. "Parents must know what is collected, where it is stored and whether it will ever be used beyond improving their own child’s experience,” says Aggarwal.
This does not make Cradlewise sinister. It makes the company consequential.
A smart crib operates in a setting where mistakes, security failures and vague permissions carry a different emotional weight from a malfunctioning shopping app. Parents deserve exceptionally clear answers about default settings, retention periods, overseas transfers, model training and the deletion of their child’s information.
Investors should demand the same clarity. Data can deepen a moat. Mishandling it can drain trust faster than a rocking crib can restore sleep.
What Will Investors Wake Up To?
Cradlewise has built something genuinely inventive.
It identified an ancient problem, combined Indian engineering with American consumer spending and converted a desperate parental desire into a premium product. Sam Altman has publicly recommended the crib. The company has assembled experienced venture investors, established manufacturing in Pune and accumulated a dataset that a new competitor cannot quickly reproduce.
The unanswered question concerns the destination of the $12 million.
Will the money expand a business already approaching attractive hardware margins? Will it finance inventory while distribution catches up? Will it subsidise customer acquisition in new countries? Will it create cheaper products capable of moving Cradlewise beyond the luxury nursery? Or will subscriptions become the profit engine supporting a difficult hardware business?
The funding announcement offers aspiration where arithmetic is required.
Parents may understandably pay heavily for two more hours of sleep. Investors are entitled to ask how much it costs Cradlewise to manufacture those hours, acquire the family purchasing them and store the data produced overnight.
The baby may sleep through all of this. The market should not. Cradlewise has built a machine designed to wake before the child does. Its business story must now wake before scrutiny arrives.

title: HyugaLife Raises ₹100 Cr in Series A Round Led by IvyCap Ventures - Indian Startup Times
content:
India’s most trusted marketplace for authentic, lab tested proteins and supplements: sets its sights on AI-powered personalisation and offline retail expansion
Date, Mumbai: India’s most trusted marketplace for authentic proteins and supplements, HyugaLife, founded by Sachin Parikh, Anvi Shah, and Neehar Modi, has raised ₹100 Cr in its Series A funding round, led by IvyCap Ventures. The round also saw participation from First Bridge Fund. Dexter Capital served as the exclusive financial advisor for the transaction. HyugaLife has previously raised funding from marquee investors such as Peak XV and Spring Marketing Capital.
The fresh capital will be used to strengthen AI-powered personalization layers, a dark store network for quicker deliveries, and establish an offline retail presence, to build an all in service of HyugaLife’s core promise: genuine products, fairly priced, delivered fast.
HyugaLife was built on a simple conviction: India’s protein and supplements market has a trust problem. The platform addressed it with H-Tested, one of the most rigorous authenticity infrastructures in Indian e-commerce, by sourcing directly from brands, eliminating third-party sellers, and publishing independent lab reports on nutrition and heavy metals across a large part of the catalogue.
The company is now building on this with AI-led personalization, tailoring discovery to a consumer’s life stage and goals, while continuing to invest in sharp, accessible content that helps people make informed choices in a category long defined by confusion.
Today, the platform lists 450+ credible brands and over 10,000 products across proteins, supplements, health foods, and wellness, serving athletes, fitness enthusiasts, working professionals, and families across India. International cricketer KL Rahul, himself a serious athlete who understands the stakes of product integrity, is among the platform’s key investors.
“India’s protein and supplements market has a trust problem, and HyugaLife was built to address it. We’re doubling down on our authenticity guarantee by expanding lab tested offering, while investing in AI driven smart, personalized technology that meets consumers at their specific life stage and fitness phase, and enabling faster access through dark stores and offline. IvyCap and First Bridge clearly understood both the vision and its importance, making this a natural partnership.”— Sachin Parikh, Founder & CEO, HyugaLife
“HyugaLife is addressing a critical trust gap in India’s proteins and supplements market through a strong authenticity-led approach. Their focus on verified sourcing, transparent information, and AI-driven personalization creates a compelling, differentiated platform. We believe they are well-positioned to scale as a trusted omnichannel health platform in India, and we are delighted to partner with them on this journey.”— Vikram Gupta, Founder & Managing Partner, IvyCap Ventures
“HyugaLife has built something genuinely hard to replicate: consumer trust at scale, in a category where scepticism is the default. The authenticity infrastructure they have put in place is a real differentiator, and the consumer response speaks for itself. We are glad to back Sachin
and the team as they move into this next phase.”— Vishal Kumar Gupta, Co-Founder and Managing Partner, First Bridge Fund
About Hyugalife
HyugaLife is India’s most trusted marketplace for authentic proteins and supplements. Founded on the belief that Indian consumers deserve access to verified, fairly priced products, the platform sources directly from brands, with zero third-party sellers, and independently lab-tests a significant share of its catalogue through its H-Tested programme, with full reports available publicly on each product page. With 450+ brands and 10,000+ products spanning proteins, supplements, health foods, and wellness, HyugaLife serves athletes, fitness enthusiasts, working professionals, and families across India. title: HyugaLife, House of Chikankari, Mojro, Kovon, others raise early-stage funds
content:
An online marketplace for health supplements, an ethnic wear brand, a logistics player, a skilling and job-discovery platform, among other startups, have raised funds in separate rounds.
HyugaLife, a marketplace for authentic proteins and supplements, has bagged Rs 100 crore (around $10.6 million) in a funding round, led by IvyCap Ventures. The round also saw participation from First Bridge Fund.
It will use the capital to strengthen the personalisation layers and its dark store network, and establish an offline retail presence, according to a press note issued by the company. Dexter Capital was the exclusive financial advisor for this transaction.
The company, founded by Sachin Parikh, Anvi Shah and Neehar Modi, is a health and wellness-focused e-commerce platform that provides products across categories such as health supplements, sports nutrition and health foods. In 2024, it raised $1 million (then Rs 8.3 crore) in a mix of equity and debt investments from existing as well as new investors including Stride Ventures and GetVantage.
In 2023, it raised $5 million in a pre-Series A funding round from venture capital firm Peak XV Partners’ early-stage accelerator Surge, Early Spring, Arihant Patni and Aman Tekriwal and other high-net-worth individuals (HNIs). The startup is also backed by actress Katrina Kaif and cricketer KL Rahul.
House of Chikankari (HOC), a contemporary ethnic wear brand rooted in traditional Indian craftsmanship, has secured Rs 25 crore (around $2.7 million) in its Series A funding round led by Cap Alpha Ventures, formerly known as Client Associates Alternate Fund (CAAF).
The brand will use the fresh funding to expand its product portfolio, strengthen its omnichannel presence with a push into offline retail, improve working capital efficiency, and invest in team expansion and marketing, according to a press note.
HOC was set up in 2020 by Aakriti Rawal and Poonam Rawal. It blends heritage embroidery techniques with contemporary design to build a scalable ethnic wear business. The company works with a network of over 10,000 women artisans across India, and has served over 2 lakh customers to date, including in more than 20 countries.
Mojro Technologies Pvt. Ltd, a logistics company using AI for supply chain optimisation, has closed its Series A round securing $5.5 million (around Rs 52 crore), with Dallas Venture Capital (DVC) joining as a new investor. This includes a previously announced $3 million investment led by IAN Alpha Fund with participation from 1Crowd, along with a $2.5 million extension by DVC.
The startup will use the capital to accelerate Mojro’s global expansion and drive product innovation, according to a company issued statement.
Mojro was founded in 2016 by Kishan Aswath, Amit Kulkarni, and Ranganath Seetharamu. It offers a logistics optimisation engine for mid- to large enterprises in sectors such as CPG, retail, courier express and parcel, dairy, and e-commerce. It helps customers save on logistics costs.
Kovon, a cross-border workforce mobility platform, has raised $250,000 (around Rs 2.4 crore) in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners.
It will deploy the fresh funds in product and platform development, strengthening employer partnerships globally, expanding candidate acquisition, and building out the skilling and training ecosystem. The company also plans to hire across technology, operations, and partnerships, according to a statement issued by the company.
Bengaluru-based Kovon offers an end-to-end platform spanning job discovery, upskilling, financing and placement. It was founded by Bibartan Roy and Swayamjeet Das in 2025, with the aim to enable global employment access for India’s blue and grey collar workforce across sectors such as healthcare, hospitality, construction and logistics.
novio
Credilio Financial Technologies’ consumer application novio has secured Rs 100 crore in a Series A funding round led by Cornerstone Ventures.
Shepherd’s Hill Private Equity, ESV-Arthya AIF and Roots Ventures also participated in the round, along with Innoven Capital and Alteria Capital.
The company will use the capital to scale distribution deeper into tier II-V markets and accelerate product development, with a focus on expanding bank partnerships.
novio is a fixed deposit credit card app that targets early jobbers, small business owners, students, gig workers and freelancers, offering access to a premium RuPay credit card.
It was founded in 2020 by Aditya Gupta, Sandeep Ghule, Manish Sinha, and Anand Kapadia,
Optimized Electrotech
Optimized Electrotech, an electro-optics company that develops indigenously-designed and manufactured surveillance systems, has raised Rs 35 crore in a round led by Exfinity Venture Partners.
Blume Ventures, Mela Ventures, and Venture Catalysts also participated in the round.
The company is now aiming to move beyond ground-based systems to build space-led intelligence infrastructure.
Founded in 2017, it builds high-end electro-optic surveillance systems for strategic and commercial buyers.

title: Nutrition Supplements Marketplace HyugaLife Raises ₹100 Cr
content: Protein and supplements marketplace HyugaLife has raised ₹100 Cr ($10.6 Mn) in its Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures, with participation from First Bridge Fund. The startup said it will use the capital to strengthen AI-driven personalisation features for users, expand its dark store network, and establish an offline presence. Founded in 2021 by Sachin Parikh, Anvi Shah and Neehar Modi, HyugaLife operates an ecommerce marketplace for health and wellness products such as herbal supplements, sports nutrition, weight management, fitness accessories, among others. The startup claims to offer more than 10,000 products across nine different categories from over 450 brands, catering to a broad spectrum of consumers, including athletes, professionals, and families. “We’re doubling down on our authenticity guarantee by expanding lab tested offerings, while investing in AI-driven smart, personalised technology that meets consumers at their specific life stage and fitness phase, and enabling faster access through dark stores and offline,” HyugaLife cofounder and CEO Parikh said. HyugaLife also offers a “H-Tested” programme that assures authenticity of products listed on its platform, through third-party labs adhering to NABL and FSSAI standards to assess their protein and nutrient values. The startup also sells self-manufactured products like creatine, whey protein, among others, under the Hyuga brand. Without disclosing the capital raised so far, HyugaLife claimed that it is backed by Peak XV and Spring Marketing Capital, alongside cricketer KL Rahul since its inception. The development comes at a time when there is a heightened consumer demand for wellness products in the market, benefitting brands operating in the health and wellness space. Since the start of this year, investors have backed brands like Mosaic Wellness, Fullife Healthcare and Dhun Wellness betting on this growing demand. Meanwhile, Mumbai-based pharmaceutical company USV signed an agreement to acquire 79% stake in Wellbeing Nutrition for ₹1,583 Cr ($174.7 Mn) in an all-cash deal, earlier in February.

title: From Plix to 4700BC: A look at the kinds of brands Marico has been acquiring
content:
From plant-based nutrition to gourmet popcorn and male grooming, Marico is assembling a portfolio of consumer brands that extends well beyond its traditional FMCG strongholds. The strategy is beginning to deliver growth, although the financial performance of its acquisitions remains uneven.
The Mumbai-headquartered company reported consolidated revenue of Rs 13,611 crore in FY26, up 26% year on year, while recurring consolidated net profit after tax and minority interest rose 11% to Rs 1,762 crore. Its newer businesses are an increasingly important part of the growth story, with nutrition emerging as a standout performer and some food brands continuing to struggle with profitability.
Marico’s premium and digital brands contributed 37% of revenue in FY26, compared with 27% in FY20. The company wants this share to reach 50% by FY30, as it looks to acquisitions, strategic investments and newer consumer categories to broaden its business.
Here is a closer look at the brands Marico has acquired or invested in, and what their latest financial performance tells us.
1. Plix: Betting on plant-based wellness
Plix, owned by Satiya Nutraceuticals, operates in the plant-based nutrition and wellness segment, with products positioned around everyday health and personal care needs. Marico acquired a majority stake in the business and subsequently increased its holding to 84.09% through additional investments of Rs 1,012.
The move gives Marico a stronger presence in a segment where consumers are increasingly being offered products that combine wellness, nutrition and beauty. Plix also adds a digital-first brand to Marico’s portfolio, broadening its reach beyond conventional FMCG distribution and categories.
2. Cosmix Wellness: Moving deeper into functional nutrition
Marico acquired a 60% stake in Bengaluru-based Cosmix Wellness in early 2026, in a transaction valued at Rs 375 crore. The startup operates in plant-based protein and functional nutrition, catering to consumers looking for alternatives to conventional nutritional supplements.
The investment strengthens Marico’s presence in the nutrition market, particularly in products built around specific consumer needs rather than mass-market food staples. Cosmix also gives the company a foothold in a segment where product innovation, online communities and specialised consumer positioning can be important to brand building.
3. 4700BC: Expanding into premium snacking
Marico acquired a controlling stake in 4700BC, the gourmet popcorn and snacking brand for Rs 227 crore, buying out PVR INOX’s stake in the business.
4700BC operates in a segment that sits at the intersection of packaged food, premiumisation and indulgence. Unlike traditional mass-market snacks, gourmet popcorn allows brands to compete through distinctive flavours, packaging and an elevated consumption experience.
4. Beardo: Building a stronger presence in male grooming
Marico first acquired a 45% stake in Beardo in 2017, before subsequently moving to full ownership of the male grooming brand.
Beardo built its identity around products such as beard oils, grooming essentials and styling products, targeting men seeking specialised personal care offerings. Its positioning also helped it stand apart from more conventional mass-market grooming brands.
The acquisition was an early example of Marico’s willingness to use acquisitions to enter emerging consumer categories rather than rely exclusively on in-house brand development. Beardo gave the company access to a focused grooming proposition and a brand built around a clearly defined consumer segment.
5. True Elements: Tapping into healthy breakfast and snacking
Marico acquired a controlling stake in True Elements, a brand focused on clean-label breakfast foods and healthier snacking options. In 2025, Marico acquired 100% stake in the brand for Rs 138 crore.
Its portfolio sits within the broader shift towards products marketed around ingredient transparency, nutrition and convenient everyday consumption. Breakfast cereals, seeds, muesli and related products allow the brand to address consumers seeking alternatives to conventional packaged breakfast options.
6. Just Herbs: Strengthening its natural beauty portfolio
Just Herbs is an Ayurvedic and natural personal care brand backed by Marico. Its positioning combines traditional Indian ingredients and beauty practices with contemporary skincare and haircare products.
The brand offers Marico another route into beauty and personal care, a market where consumers are presented with a growing range of specialised brands built around ingredients, product philosophies and targeted benefits.
Just Herbs also fits into a broader portfolio approach in which Marico can address different consumer preferences through separate brands, rather than trying to stretch a single name across every beauty and personal care segment.

title: VERTICES PARTNERS advises PLIX as Marico acquires additional stake for ₹1,012 crore

title: Marico increases ASP investments as it doubles down on brand building
content:
Marico has increased its advertising, sales and promotion (ASP) investments in Q2 FY27 as it continued to invest in brand building and growth initiatives.
In its quarterly update for the period ended September 30, 2026, the company said domestic demand remained resilient, with its India business reporting strong underlying volume performance. Parachute Coconut Oil recorded early-teens volume growth, and the same has been attributed to the brand equity, consumer trust, and its supply chain advantage.
Value Added Hair Oils also continued its strong performance, touching the twenties for the sixth consecutive quarter. The company attributed this to investments in the mid- and premium segments, Project SETU's direct reach and the expansion of its Almond category.
Marico said its foods, premium personal care and digital-first brands also continued to add to portfolio diversification. Saffola Oils, meanwhile, recorded mid-single-digit price-led growth, while volumes declined as the company maintained profitability thresholds and rationalised select variants.
International markets recorded constant-currency growth in the teens, led by Vietnam, the Middle East and South Africa. Bangladesh showed a marginal sequential improvement despite a high base and inflationary pressures.
At the consolidated level, Marico expects double-digit revenue growth in Q2 FY27. Gross margin is also expected to improve strongly year on year, supported by the portfolio mix and lower copra costs. Operating profit is expected to grow in the mid-twenties.
“ASP investments increased significantly as we continued to invest in brand building and growth initiatives,” the company said.
Marico expects its first-half performance to surpass its near-term guidance across key financial parameters, supported by its core franchises and newer growth engines. The company continues to target sustainable, profitable, volume-led growth over the medium term.

title: Marico Limited (NSE:MARICO) Raises Satiya Nutraceuticals Holding to 84.09% Through ₹1,012.03 Crore Deal
content:
Highlights
- Marico has completed the acquisition of an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals.
- The latest transaction carries a cash consideration of ₹1,012.03 crore.
- Marico’s aggregate holding has increased from 60% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis.
- The company retains the right to acquire the remaining 14.09% stake in July 2027.
- The transaction deepens Marico’s presence in health, wellness, nutrition and personal care.
Marico Limited (NSE:MARICO), a consumer products company with businesses spanning personal care, foods and wellness categories, has increased its ownership in Satiya Nutraceuticals Private Limited. The company completed the acquisition of an additional 24.09% stake on 5 October 2026 for ₹1,012.03 crore in cash. Following the transaction, Marico’s aggregate holding in the subsidiary has increased from 60% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis.
Additional Stake Expands Marico’s Ownership
The latest acquisition represents another stage in Marico’s investment in Satiya Nutraceuticals, which owns the plant-based nutrition and personal-care brand Plix.
Prior to the transaction, Marico held a 60% stake in the business on a fully diluted basis. The additional 24.09% interest takes the total holding to 84.09%, giving Marico a larger economic interest in the subsidiary while maintaining its existing control.
The ₹1,012.03 crore consideration for the latest tranche was paid in cash. Following completion, the aggregate consideration paid by Marico for its 84.09% holding stands at ₹1,392.07 crore.
Acquisition Journey Began in 2023
Marico first entered Satiya Nutraceuticals in July 2023 by acquiring an initial stake and obtaining control over the business. Subsequent transactions gradually increased its ownership.
By May 2025, Marico had raised its stake to 60% on a fully diluted basis. The latest transaction continues this phased acquisition approach rather than representing entry into a completely new business.
This gradual ownership structure has allowed Marico to increase its participation in the company over multiple stages while continuing to integrate the brand within its wider consumer portfolio.
Plix Adds Health and Wellness Exposure
Satiya Nutraceuticals operates in the health, wellness, nutrition and personal-care segments through Plix. Its portfolio includes products positioned around plant-based nutrition and related consumer wellness categories.
The business gives Marico exposure to categories that differ from its traditional mass-market consumer products. Health and wellness has become an increasingly important area for established consumer companies seeking to participate in changing consumption patterns.
The acquisition therefore aligns with Marico’s broader effort to expand its presence in value-added foods, nutrition and premium consumer categories.
Remaining Stake Planned for July 2027
Following the latest acquisition, 14.09% of Satiya Nutraceuticals remains outside Marico’s ownership.
Under the amended definitive agreements, Marico is expected to acquire this remaining stake in July 2027, subject to the agreed terms and conditions. The base consideration for the remaining interest is up to ₹592 crore, with the final amount also subject to applicable milestones and transaction conditions.
If completed as planned, the transaction would further increase Marico’s ownership in the business. Until then, the latest completed deal leaves its holding at 84.09% on a fully diluted basis.
Why the Phased Structure Matters
A phased acquisition enables a company to increase ownership over time rather than purchasing the entire business in a single transaction.
Such structures may link future consideration to agreed milestones and allow ownership to increase as the business progresses through different stages. In Marico’s case, the arrangement has resulted in multiple stake increases since the original investment.
For readers, it is important to distinguish between the stake already acquired and the portion planned for future purchase. The 24.09% acquisition has been completed, while the remaining 14.09% transaction is scheduled for a later period and remains subject to the agreed conditions.
Portfolio Diversification Remains the Central Theme
Marico has increasingly expanded beyond its established consumer categories into foods, wellness and digital-first brands. The additional investment in Satiya Nutraceuticals fits within that diversification strategy.
Acquiring a larger interest provides Marico with greater participation in the future development of the business while keeping the existing brand within its consolidated portfolio.
The development is therefore primarily a corporate ownership and portfolio-expansion event rather than a change to Marico’s core listed-company structure.
Key Insights
Marico’s acquisition of an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals increases its holding to 84.09% and represents a further step in a transaction that began in 2023.
The ₹1,012.03 crore cash consideration significantly increases Marico’s investment in the business, while the remaining 14.09% stake is planned for acquisition in July 2027.
The transaction expands Marico’s exposure to health, wellness, nutrition and personal-care categories and demonstrates its continued use of acquisitions to broaden its consumer portfolio.
FAQs
Q: How much additional stake has Marico acquired in Satiya Nutraceuticals?
A: Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake.
Q: What was the consideration for the latest acquisition?
A: The transaction was completed for ₹1,012.03 crore in cash.
Q: What is Marico’s holding after the transaction?
A: Marico now holds 84.09% on a fully diluted basis.
Q: Does Marico plan to acquire the remaining stake?
A: Yes. The remaining 14.09% stake is planned to be acquired in July 2027, subject to agreed terms and conditions.
Q: What business does Satiya Nutraceuticals operate?
A: It operates in plant-based nutrition, health, wellness and personal-care categories through the Plix brand.

title: Marico edges lower as Plix buyout, strong Q2 cues stir midday trade
content:
Shares of Marico Limited were marginally in the red on Tuesday but drew active midday interest on the bourses, a day after the FMCG major filed two disclosures, a pre-quarter business update and a significant acquisition in the direct-to-consumer nutrition brand Plix.
At 12.27 pm on the NSE, Marico (MARICO) was quoted at ₹789.00, down ₹1.00 or 0.13 per cent from its previous close of ₹790.00. The stock opened at ₹796.95, touching its intraday high at the open, before slipping to a low of ₹784.50. Traded volume stood at 5.95 lakh shares worth ₹46.87 crore by midday, with buy orders accounting for 55.39 per cent of the total order flow. Deliverable quantity was 64.08 per cent of traded volume, pointing to relatively firm underlying conviction in the counter. The stock’s total market capitalisation stood at ₹1,02,345.56 crore.
Marico increased its aggregate stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, owner of plant-based brand Plix, from 60 per cent to 84.09 per cent on a fully diluted basis. The company paid ₹1,012.03 crore for the current tranche of 24.09 per cent, taking the total consideration for the 84.09 per cent stake to ₹1,392.07 crore. A residual 14.09 per cent stake is expected to be acquired in July 2027 for a base consideration of up to ₹592 crore, plus performance-linked payouts.
Monday’s Q2 FY27 pre-quarter update also provided positive cues. Consolidated revenue is expected to grow in double digits, with Parachute Coconut Oil posting early-teens volume growth and value-added hair oils growing in the twenties for the sixth straight quarter. International business delivered constant-currency growth in the teens. Operating profit is expected to expand in the mid-twenties year-on-year.
Street views, however, remain divided. HSBC maintained a Buy with a target price of ₹1,020, while CLSA holds an Underperform with a ₹703 target on valuation concerns. JM Financial retained its Buy but trimmed the target to ₹940 from ₹1,015, citing sector-wide PE derating. The stock’s 52-week high of ₹889.10 was hit on July 30, 2026, against a low of ₹703.95 recorded a year ago.

title: Marico steps up brand-building investments in Q2 FY27
content:
New Delhi: Marico stepped up investments behind brand building and growth initiatives in the September quarter, extending the higher marketing intensity seen in the previous quarter.
In its Q2 FY27 quarterly update, the company said advertising and sales promotion (ASP) investments “increased significantly” during the quarter as it continued to invest behind brand building and growth initiatives. Marico has not yet disclosed the rupee value of the Q2 spend; the detailed numbers will come with its quarterly financial results.
The increase follows a sharp rise in Q1 FY27, when Marico spent Rs 327 crore on advertising and sales promotion, up 25% from the restated Rs 261 crore in Q1 FY26. ASP accounted for around 8.3% of consolidated revenue in the June quarter.
Marico had said the higher investment was aimed at strengthening the long-term equity of its brands.
For context, Marico had originally reported Rs 345 crore of ASP expenditure in Q2 FY26, up 19% from Rs 290 crore in Q2 FY25. ASP then accounted for 9.9% of revenue.
That figure, however, was reported under the earlier accounting presentation.
Beginning Q1 FY27, Marico changed the accounting treatment of certain customer-related advertising and promotional expenses, netting them off against revenue instead of reporting them under advertising and sales promotion expenses. Comparative periods have been restated accordingly.
The Rs 345 crore originally reported for Q2 FY26 should therefore not be directly compared with the Q2 FY27 number until Marico publishes the corresponding restated Q2 FY26 figure.
The higher brand-building push comes as Marico's India business delivered another quarter of strong volume growth.
Underlying volume growth touched double digits in Q2 FY27. Parachute Coconut Oil accelerated to early-teens volume growth, which the company attributed to the brand's equity, consumer trust and its supply-chain advantage.
Value Added Hair Oils recorded growth in the twenties for another quarter, extending its strong run to six consecutive quarters. Marico said investments in the mid- and premium segments, increased direct reach through Project SETU and growth in the almond category supported the performance.
Saffola Oils delivered mid-single-digit price-led growth, although volumes declined as Marico focused on maintaining threshold profitability and rationalised supply of select variants.
Foods and Premium Personal Care, including digital-first brands and shampoo, also sustained their growth momentum as the company continued to scale businesses beyond its core franchises.
The higher marketing investment is also in line with Marico's broader portfolio strategy, under which it has been building premium personal care, foods and digital-first businesses such as Beardo, Plix, True Elements, Just Herbs and Cosmix alongside established brands such as Parachute and Saffola.
In Q1 FY27, Marico had said its Foods portfolio grew 43% and crossed an annualised revenue run-rate of Rs 1,300 crore, while Premium Personal Care reached an annualised run-rate of around Rs 450 crore.
For Q2, Marico expects consolidated revenue to grow in double digits, supported by its core, digital and international portfolios.
The international business delivered constant-currency growth in the teens, led by Vietnam, the Middle East and South Africa. Bangladesh showed a marginal sequential improvement but continued to contend with elevated inflation and a high base.
On the cost side, crude-linked derivatives became more expensive, while copra prices remained around 35% below peak levels.
Marico expects gross margins to improve strongly year-on-year, helped by portfolio mix and lower copra prices. Despite the higher brand investments, it expects operating profit to grow in the mid-twenties during the quarter.
The company said its performance in the first half of the year puts it on course to surpass its near-term guidance across key financial parameters.

title: Marico takes Plix holding to 84.09%, pays Rs 1,012 crore for latest tranche
content:
New Delhi: Marico has increased its shareholding in Satiya Nutraceuticals, the company that owns the plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix, from 60% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis.
According to a stock exchange filing, Marico acquired a 24.09% stake for Rs 1,012.03 crore in cash. The purchase was completed on Monday, October 5.
With this, the total amount Marico has paid for its 84.09% holding in Satiya Nutraceuticals stands at Rs 1,392.07 crore.
The purchase is part of definitive agreements under which Marico will acquire 38.18% of Satiya Nutraceuticals in tranches from its Founders and certain other shareholders. The company had earlier held a right to buy the 40% it did not own.
The remaining 14.09% is scheduled to be acquired in July 2027, subject to the terms of the agreements. The price for that tranche will be decided at the time. It will comprise a base consideration of up to Rs 592 crore and an additional amount linked to milestones.
Satiya Nutraceuticals was incorporated on February 13, 2020 and is headquartered in Mumbai. It operates in the health, wellness and personal care space and has a wholly owned subsidiary, Juizo Advisory.
The company's consolidated turnover was Rs 864.31 crore in FY26, against Rs 432.84 crore in FY25 and Rs 155.32 crore in FY24.
According to Marico, the investment in Satiya Nutraceuticals has widened its addressable market in value-added foods and nutrition, and extended its presence in personal care and wellness categories.

title: Marico Raises Plix Stake To 84.09% With Rs 1,012 Cr Acquisition
content:
Marico has acquired an additional 24.09 per cent stake in plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix for Rs 1,012.03 crore in an all-cash transaction, taking its total holding in the company to 84.09 per cent.
As per a media report, the latest transaction is part of an agreement under which Marico will acquire a total 38.18 per cent stake in Plix from its founders and certain other shareholders.
Marico will acquire the remaining 14.09 per cent stake in July 2027. The consideration for this tranche will include a base amount of up to Rs 592 crore, along with additional payments linked to the achievement of certain milestones.
Marico said its investment in Plix parent Satiya Nutraceuticals and its wholly owned subsidiary Juzio has helped broaden its addressable market across value-added foods and nutrition, while strengthening its presence in the personal care and wellness segments.
Founded in 2020 by Satiya and Zaveri, Plix Life is a Mumbai-based D2C startup that offers plant-based nutrition products, including workout supplements, ingestible sunscreens, hair growth serums and skincare products.
The consolidated revenue of Plix's parent company nearly doubled to Rs 864.31 crore in FY26 from Rs 432.84 crore in FY25.
Marico had acquired a 37.75 per cent stake in Plix for Rs 369.01 crore in July 2023 and subsequently acquired another 25.25 per cent of the company's paid-up share capital by May 2025. Plix's cap table had included investors such as Guild Capital and RPSG Ventures.
The latest transaction is part of Marico's broader strategy to expand into high-growth consumer categories beyond its established food, personal care and consumer product portfolio.
Marico has made several acquisitions in 2026. It acquired a 93.27 per cent stake in gourmet popcorn brand 4700BC's parent Zea Maize from PVR INOX for Rs 226.8 crore. In February, it acquired a 60 per cent stake in Bengaluru-based plant-based protein startup Cosmix Wellness for Rs 226 crore. It also acquired a 75 per cent stake in Vietnam-based Skinetiq Joint Stock Company for an estimated Rs 262-350 crore.
The growth of Plix comes as large FMCG companies continue to expand into newer consumer categories, particularly health, nutrition, personal care and wellness.
ITC recently completed the acquisition of 100 per cent of Yoga Bar's parent Sproutlife Foods by purchasing the remaining 52.5 per cent stake for around Rs 645 crore.
Emami had earlier acquired a 60 per cent stake in IncNut Digital, the parent company of D2C beauty and personal care brands Vedix and SkinKraft, for up to Rs 321 crore in an all-cash transaction.
Hindustan Unilever also acquired the remaining 49 per cent stake in OZiva's parent Zywie Ventures for Rs 824 crore in February.

title: Marico Acquires Additional 24.09% Stake in Plix Parent for Rs 1,012.03 Crore
content:
FMCG major Marico has acquired an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, the parent company of plant-based nutrition and personal care brand Plix, for Rs 1,012.03 crore.
The acquisition, completed on October 5, 2026, has increased Marico’s stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals from 60% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis. The transaction was carried out in cash.
Marico had earlier acquired a 60% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals through multiple transactions and had the right to acquire the remaining 40% stake under definitive agreements.
As part of the latest transaction, Marico had entered into definitive agreements to acquire a total 38.18% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals from the founders and certain other shareholders. The latest tranche involved the acquisition of 24.09% of the company.
The remaining 14.09% stake is expected to be acquired in July 2027, subject to the terms and conditions of the definitive agreements. The consideration for this remaining stake will include a base consideration of up to Rs 592 crore, along with additional consideration linked to milestones and other terms under the agreements.
Following the latest transaction, Marico’s aggregate consideration for its 84.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals stands at Rs 1,392.07 crore.
Satiya Nutraceuticals was incorporated in February 2020 and is headquartered in Mumbai. The company owns The Plant Fix, or Plix, a plant-based nutrition and personal care brand operating across the health, wellness and personal care segments.
Satiya Nutraceuticals reported consolidated turnover of Rs 864.31 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 432.84 crore in FY25 and Rs 155.32 crore in FY24.
Marico has said that its investment in Satiya Nutraceuticals has expanded its total addressable market in value-added foods and nutrition while strengthening its presence in personal care and wellness categories.
The acquisition is part of Marico’s broader efforts to expand its portfolio of digital-first consumer brands. Its portfolio includes Beardo, Just Herbs and Skinetiq in beauty, as well as True Elements in wellness. In 2026, Marico also acquired 4700BC and Cosmix, adding healthy snacking and plant-based nutrition brands to its portfolio.
With the latest acquisition, Marico has further increased its ownership of Satiya Nutraceuticals and Plix, while retaining an agreement to acquire the remaining 14.09% stake in July 2027, subject to the agreed terms and conditions.

title: Marico Acquires Additional 24.09% Stake In Plix Parent Satiya For ₹10.1 Billion
content:
Marico Acquires Additional 24.09% Stake In Plix Parent Satiya For ₹10.1 Billion
Marico has strengthened its fast-growing wellness and nutrition portfolio by acquiring an additional 24.09% stake in Plix parent Satiya Nutraceuticals for ₹1,012.03 crore, bringing its total ownership to 84.09%. This strategic consolidation comes as Plix continues its rapid expansion, having doubled its consolidated turnover to ₹864.31 crore in FY26. The final 14.09% stake is scheduled for acquisition in July 2027 for a base consideration of up to ₹592 crore alongside milestone-linked performance payments.
Market snapshot: Marico Limited has completed the acquisition of an additional 24.09% stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals Private Limited, the parent entity of plant-based wellness brand Plix, for a cash consideration of ₹1,012.03 crore. The transaction, completed on October 5, 2026, raises Marico's total holding in Satiya from 60.00% to 84.09% on a fully diluted basis. Additionally, the company has entered into an agreement to acquire the remaining 14.09% stake in July 2027.

- Balance Sheet Strength: Completing a ₹1,012.03 crore tranche entirely in cash emphasizes Marico's resilient cash flows and liquidity.
SAHI Perspective
Marico's scale-up of Satiya Nutraceuticals represents a highly disciplined execution of its premiumization and digital-first diversification strategy. By staging the transaction in tranches, Marico has managed capital allocation prudently. The outstanding financial trajectory of Plix—nearly doubling its revenue in FY26 to ₹864.31 crore and achieving a sharp increase in profitability—justifies the valuation of approximately 5x FY26 sales and reflects a successful integration of digital-first brands into Marico's wider distribution network.
Market Implications
The transaction highlights the intensifying consolidation in the Indian wellness and D2C personal care space, where established FMCG players are aggressively scaling acquired digital-first brands to build high-margin portfolios. Marico's deepening integration of Plix is expected to enhance its overall operating margins over the medium term, as these premium nutrition and personal care segments scale up and leverage Marico's offline reach.
Trading Signals

The cash-funded consolidation of Plix, which doubled its revenue to ₹864.31 crore in FY26, enhances Marico's premium portfolio. Combined with robust double-digit volume growth in domestic business in its Q2 FY27 update, this supports a strong positive outlook.

- Successful margin expansion as digital-first brands like Plix and Cosmix scale offline
- Movement of raw material costs, particularly copra prices, which corrected 45% from peak and supported Q1 performance

Industry Context
The Indian consumer goods and wellness industry is witnessing a structural shift towards health, wellness, and preventive nutrition. Traditional FMCG giants are actively building out digital-first portfolios to capture premium consumer segments. Marico's portfolio of acquired digital and premium brands, including Beardo, 4700BC, Cosmix, True Elements, and Plix, generated a combined ₹1,552 crore in FY26 revenue, underscoring the growing importance of these new engines alongside core franchises like Parachute and Saffola.

- Volatility in raw material prices, particularly agricultural inputs, which can impact gross margins of the value-added food segments.
- Intense competition in the plant-based nutrition and wellness space from both established FMCG players and nimble digital-first startups.
Recent Developments
On October 5, 2026, Marico released its Q2 FY27 quarterly update, reporting resilient domestic demand and double-digit underlying volume growth in the India business. Additionally, Parachute Coconut Oil accelerated its volume growth into the early teens, driven by a favorable copra cycle. In July 2026, Marico's detailed subsidiary financials showed its acquired portfolio reached a combined revenue of ₹1,552 crore in FY26.
Closing Insight
Marico's consolidation of Satiya Nutraceuticals marks a crucial milestone in its transition toward a modern, diversified FMCG player. By scaling digital-first brands like Plix, Marico is effectively future-proofing its portfolio against shifting retail dynamics.

MUMBAI: Marico is taking a bigger bite of the wellness market, raising its stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals, which owns the PLIX brand, to 84.09 per cent through a Rs 1,012.03 crore acquisition.
The company said on 5 October that it had completed the acquisition of an additional 24.09 per cent stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals on a fully diluted basis. Marico previously held a 60 per cent stake in the company.
The latest transaction is part of definitive agreements under which Marico has agreed to acquire an aggregate additional 38.18 per cent stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals from its founders and certain other shareholders in tranches.
With the latest purchase, Marico’s aggregate consideration for its 84.09 per cent stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals stands at Rs 1,392.07 crore.
The remaining 14.09 per cent stake is scheduled to be acquired in July 2027, subject to the terms and conditions of the definitive agreements. The consideration for this tranche will comprise a base amount of up to Rs 592 crore, along with additional consideration linked to specified milestones.
The acquisition is being made entirely for cash. No governmental or regulatory approvals are required for the transaction, according to Marico’s disclosure.
Satiya Nutraceuticals, incorporated in February 2020 and headquartered in Mumbai, owns The Plant Fix, or PLIX, a plant-based nutrition and personal care brand.
Marico said its investment in the business has expanded its total addressable market in value-added foods and nutrition, while strengthening its presence in the fast-growing personal care and wellness categories.
