title: Marico bought two brands in 90 days and spent Rs 1,300 crore on ads; here’s the bet it is making
content:
New Delhi: Ten years ago, Marico was almost mostly a coconut oil and edible oils company. Today, it owns stakes in a plant-based protein brand, a gourmet popcorn label, a functional wellness startup, and a men's grooming company.
Marico’s digital-first brand portfolio has grown from an exit annual run rate (ARR) of Rs 400 crore in Q3FY24 to Rs 1,100 crore by the end of FY26, nearly tripling in roughly two years. The company now targets this portfolio to reach 2.5 times its FY24 base by FY27, and 5 times by FY30.
The portfolio currently comprises Beardo, Just Herbs, True Elements, Plix, Cosmix and 4700BC, spanning men's grooming, skincare, health foods, plant-based nutrition, functional wellness and premium snacking.
How did Marico get here?
Marico has built this portfolio through a series of targeted acquisitions of founder-led, digitally-native businesses.
In Q1FY26, it raised its stake in Plix to 60% on a fully diluted basis. In Q2FY26, it acquired the remaining 46.02% stake in True Elements, a health food brand founded in 2015 by Puru Gupta and Sreejith Moolayil, making it a wholly owned subsidiary with effect from October 17, 2025.
Just Herbs was merged directly into Marico's standalone operations in October 2025. In Q4FY26, Marico acquired a 94.02% stake in 4700BC and a 60% stake in Cosmix, both completed within the January-March 2026 quarter.
Five brands, multiple acquisitions, all within roughly eighteen months.
Catching up with the timeline
Back in early 2024, Saugata Gupta, MD & CEO, had said that the “biggest improvement in D2C business has been in terms of the burn rate,” and that the entire diversified portfolio of food and digital brands would become “meaningfully profitable by 2027.”
Two years later, that timeline is holding. Marico has guided for double-digit EBITDA margins in the digital-first portfolio by the end of FY27, expanding to teens by FY30.
In FY24, Gupta had said Beardo was already operationally profitable, while Just Herbs and True Elements were expected to hit EBITDA break-even in FY25.
Plix, the plant-based nutrition brand, was expected to generate Rs 200 crore in revenue in FY25, with margins higher than the overall foods category.
The combined profit share of Foods and digital-first brands in India has now moved to approximately 5x of FY20 levels in FY26. Marico expects this to reach 10x of FY20 levels by FY30.
The bigger, strategic picture
The scale-up of digital-first brands is part of Marico's broader strategy, which seems to reduce exposure to commodity-linked businesses.
In FY20, commodity-linked categories, primarily coconut oil and edible oils, made up 73% of its overall portfolio.
These are businesses where profitability is directly tied to raw material prices, particularly copra. When copra prices rise sharply, as they did in FY26, up 57% on-year, margins get squeezed.
Marico's EBITDA margin fell 265 basis points in FY26 to 17.1%, largely because of this.
Digital-first brands do not carry this risk. They are premium, margin-accretive, and largely insulated from commodity price swings.
Gupta had noted in FY24 that most digital-first products are gross margin-accretive, and the company did not expect a significant impact on overall EBITDA margin with a scale-up in these businesses.
Numbers aligned
By FY26, the premium and digital share of Marico's portfolio has already risen to 37%, from 27% in FY20. The target, notably, is 50% by FY30.
To support the scale-up of its digital-first and food portfolios, Marico has also been increasing its advertising and sales promotion spends. Consolidated ad spends for FY26 stood at Rs 1,300 crore, up 15% from Rs 1,128 crore in FY25.
At a consolidated level, Marico posted revenues of Rs 13,611 crore in FY26, up 26% year-on-year, the highest growth in 14 years. It is targeting Rs 15,000 crore in FY27 and Rs 20,000 crore by FY30.
The digital-first portfolio will not get it there alone. But the trajectory, from Rs 400 crore in FY24 to Rs 1,100 crore in FY26, with a target of 2.5x FY24 by FY27, suggests it will carry a lot more weight than it did just two years ago.
In 2017, Marico bought a men's grooming brand called Beardo. In 2026, it owns popcorn, protein, and a wellness shot. Whatever it buys in 2030, it probably will not need copra to make it.

title: Marico shifts over half its ad spends online; allocates 100% to Beardo, Plix, digital-first brands
content:
ADVERTISEMENT
FMCG major Marico Ltd is ramping up its shift towards new-age digital brands, accompanied by an increase in advertising investments amid improvements in its profitability.
During the investor call for the fourth quarter, Chief Executive Officer Saugata Gupta stated that 55% of Marico's core advertising spend has been directed towards digital media, and 100% towards all its acquisitions, including Beardo, Plix, Skinetiq, Cosmix, and True Elements.
Marico spent Rs 1,300 crore on advertising and promotional activities in fiscal year 2026, up 15% from Rs 1,128 crore a year earlier, accounting for 9.6% of its revenue.
The company's push into premium personal care and wellness is also beginning to yield results. Two of its three key digital acquisitions, such as Cosmix and Skinetiq, have already turned profitable, said Gupta.
Skinetiq clocked margins in the mid-20s and Cosmix in the high teens. Plix, which forms a significant part of the digital portfolio, is also seeing a steady improvement in operating margins.
Marico's digital-first premium personal care portfolio exited FY26 with an annual run rate above Rs 1,100 crore. The company expects this segment to achieve double-digit EBITDA by the end of fiscal year 2027 and scale up to high-teen margins by FY2030, driven by premiumization. Gupta projected that Marico's digital portfolio could collectively generate Rs 4,000 crore in revenue by FY30
Marico's food business has also gained scale, closing FY26 with revenues exceeding Rs 1,000 crore. The portfolio now spans multiple segments, including health and wellness, clean-label foods, modern breakfast and snacking, gourmet offerings, and functional nutrition.
Marico reported revenue from operations of Rs 13,611 crore in FY26, clocking a 26% year-on-year increase, its highest growth in 14 years.
The company's domestic business delivered an underlying volume growth of 8%, a seven-year high, while international operations posted 20% constant currency growth, also the strongest in over a decade.
Marico’s contribution of foods and premium personal care portfolios, including digital-first brands, to its India revenues stood at about 23% in FY26. This is expected to rise around 27% and further to 33% by FY30.
Gupta has also projected that the premiumization strategy, coupled with scale benefits and operating efficiencies, will drive improvement in overall margins over the next few years.

title: Premiumisation to help sustain strong volume, revenue growth: Marico MD
content:
"Large, organised players are in a far better position compared to smaller players. During any crisis, the strong gets stronger and the weak gets weaker," Gupta added, due to superior supply chain control and balance sheets while smaller firms are more exposed to working capital stress. "Protection against inflation also means your ability to stock up. It's a question of working capital."
On Tuesday, Marico posted its strongest volume growth in seven years, with India business volumes rising 8% in FY26 on-year. On a consolidated basis, it reported revenue of ₹13,611 crore, up 26% in FY26. Profit after tax stood at ₹1,762 crore, growing 8% on-year. In the quarter ended March, it posted a 22% rise in revenue at ₹3,333 crore, while net profit grew 14% to ₹391 crore.
"Demand is fairly okay and we are not seeing any stress signs," Gupta said, citing rural recovery, low food inflation and affordability gains.
Copra, which accounts for roughly half of input costs, has corrected 30-35%, offsetting pressure from crude-linked inputs. "We have taken some marginal price increases already. We are prepared for slightly higher input costs," the MD and CEO said, adding that Marico had previously absorbed a 100% spike in copra without hurting profitability.
Marico expects to sustain high single-digit volume growth and deliver double-digit revenue expansion, supported by premiumisation, diversification and steady demand. "I don't see any significant reason to reduce our outlook or optimism. I don't think FMCG drastically slowed down. What has happened is some incumbents lost opportunities," Gupta said, adding that larger players are now better positioned to regain share.
Many digital-native brands, he said, struggle to scale beyond ₹500 crore due to weak distribution in general trade, an area where Marico retains a competitive edge. At the same time, Marico is leaning into emerging channels such as quick commerce, which now accounts for roughly 35-40% of its e-commerce business."We are using quick commerce as a prototyping channel," Gupta said.

title: Marico Q4 FY26: Volume Growth at 9% Beats Estimates, Co MD Targets Top Performance by FY27
content:
Marico Q4 FY26: Volume Growth at 9% Beats Estimates, Co MD Targets Top Performance by FY27
Marico Limited's Board approved audited standalone and consolidated financial results for Q4 and FY26 on May 5, 2026, with Q4 volume growth of 9% exceeding analyst estimates of 7%. Consolidated FY26 revenue from operations rose to Rs. 13,611 crore from Rs. 10,831 crore, while net profit grew to Rs. 1,813 crore from Rs. 1,658 crore. The Board recommended a final dividend of Rs. 4.00 per share, approved the 38th AGM for August 6, 2026, and completed five strategic acquisitions during FY26 including stakes in Plix, True Elements, Just Herbs, 4700BC, and Cosmix.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.
Marico Limited's Board of Directors, at its meeting held on May 5, 2026, approved the audited standalone and consolidated financial results for the quarter and financial year ended March 31, 2026. The Board also recommended a final equity dividend of Rs. 4.00 per equity share of Re. 1 each for FY25-26, subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing 38th Annual General Meeting. The statutory auditors, B S R & Co. LLP, issued their audit reports with an unmodified opinion on both standalone and consolidated financial results. Notably, Q4 FY26 volume growth came in at 9%, ahead of analyst estimates of 7%, reflecting robust domestic demand momentum. Pursuant to Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the audio recording of the earnings conference call held on May 5, 2026 is available on the Company's website, with the transcript to be published subsequently.
Business Outlook
Marico's Co MD has declared a firm commitment to achieving top performance by FY27, reinforcing the company's near-term growth priorities across geographies. The company aims for mid-teen growth in its International business by FY27, fuelled by strong market performance across its overseas operations. On the domestic front, India is anticipated to sustain continued high single-digit volume growth in FY27, underpinned by the strength of its core portfolio and recent brand acquisitions.
Key Board Decisions
Alongside the financial results, the Board approved several significant resolutions at its meeting, which commenced at 12:30 p.m. and concluded at 1:45 p.m. on May 5, 2026.
Q4 FY26 Operational Highlights
Marico's Q4 FY26 performance reflected steady top-line growth against the prior year period, with revenue and profitability broadly in line with analyst estimates. The following table presents key Q4 FY26 metrics alongside year-on-year comparisons and market estimates:
While revenue and net profit came in largely in line with estimates, EBITDA margin contracted by 120 basis points year-on-year to 15.6%, compared to 16.8% in Q4 FY25, and came in marginally below the analyst estimate of 15.8%. Volume growth, however, outperformed expectations at 9% versus the estimated 7%.
Consolidated Financial Performance
Marico's consolidated financials reflect strong year-on-year growth across key metrics for the year ended March 31, 2026. Revenue from operations grew to Rs. 13,611 crore from Rs. 10,831 crore in the prior year. Net profit for the year stood at Rs. 1,813 crore compared to Rs. 1,658 crore previously. The following table summarises the consolidated income statement highlights:
Net profit attributable to owners for FY26 stood at Rs. 1,762 crore versus Rs. 1,629 crore in FY25, while the share attributable to non-controlling interests was Rs. 51 crore compared to Rs. 29 crore in the prior year.
Consolidated Segment Performance
Marico operates across two reportable segments — India and International. The India segment remained the dominant revenue contributor, while the International segment also delivered meaningful growth.
Segment assets for India stood at Rs. 4,832 crore and International at Rs. 2,548 crore as at March 31, 2026, with unallocated assets of Rs. 2,695 crore. Segment liabilities for India were Rs. 1,774 crore and International Rs. 888 crore, with unallocated liabilities of Rs. 2,919 crore.
Standalone Financial Performance
On a standalone basis, Marico reported revenue from operations of Rs. 9,402 crore for FY26 versus Rs. 7,680 crore in FY25. Net profit for the standalone entity rose to Rs. 1,941 crore from Rs. 1,519 crore in the prior year. The standalone results for FY25 have been restated to account for the integration of Apcos Naturals Private Limited (Just Herbs) as a common control business acquisition.
Consolidated Balance Sheet Highlights
Marico's consolidated total assets grew to Rs. 10,075 crore as at March 31, 2026, from Rs. 8,332 crore as at March 31, 2025. Total equity stood at Rs. 4,494 crore versus Rs. 4,266 crore in the prior year. Cash and cash equivalents at the end of FY26 were Rs. 404 crore, up from Rs. 321 crore at the end of FY25.
On a standalone basis, total assets stood at Rs. 7,619 crore as at March 31, 2026, compared to Rs. 5,976 crore in the prior year. Total equity attributable to owners was Rs. 5,808 crore versus Rs. 4,677 crore previously, with standalone cash and cash equivalents rising to Rs. 112 crore from Rs. 41 crore.
Consolidated Cash Flow Summary
On a consolidated basis, Marico generated net cash from operating activities of Rs. 2,084 crore for FY26, compared to Rs. 1,363 crore in FY25. Net cash utilised in investing activities stood at Rs. 722 crore, while net cash utilised in financing activities was Rs. 1,279 crore. The net increase in cash and cash equivalents for FY26 was Rs. 83 crore, with closing cash and cash equivalents at Rs. 404 crore.
On a standalone basis, net cash from operating activities was Rs. 1,609 crore for FY26 versus Rs. 1,103 crore in FY25. Net cash utilised in investing activities was Rs. 534 crore and in financing activities Rs. 1,004 crore, resulting in a net increase in standalone cash and cash equivalents of Rs. 71 crore, with closing balance at Rs. 112 crore.
Key Corporate Developments
Several strategic transactions were completed during FY26 that have shaped the Group's current structure. During the quarter ended June 30, 2025, Marico acquired an additional 8.8% equity stake in Satiya Nutraceuticals Private Limited (Plix) on a fully diluted basis, taking its total stake to 60%. HW Wellness Solutions Private Limited (True Elements) was made a wholly owned subsidiary effective October 17, 2025, following the acquisition of the balance 46.02% equity capital. The business undertaking of Apcos Naturals Private Limited (Just Herbs) was vested in the Company on a going concern basis effective October 1, 2025, pursuant to voluntary liquidation. During the quarter ended March 31, 2026, the Company acquired a 93.27% equity stake in Zea Maize Private Limited (4700BC) effective January 29, 2026, subsequently increasing its stake to 94.02%. Additionally, a 60% equity stake in Cosmix Wellness Private Limited (Cosmix) was acquired effective February 5, 2026.
Company Background and Market Position
During FY25-26, Marico recorded a turnover of ₹136.1 billion (USD 1.5 billion) through its products sold in India and chosen markets in Asia and Africa. The company's domestic portfolio includes brands such as Parachute, Saffola, Hair & Care, Parachute Advansed, Nihar Naturals, Mediker, Pure Sense, Coco Soul, Revive, Set Wet, Livon, Beardo, Just Herbs, True Elements, Plix, Cosmix and 4700BC, touching the lives of 1 out of every 3 Indians. The overseas consumer products portfolio contributes approximately 24% of the Group's revenue, with international brands including Parachute, Parachute Advansed, HairCode, Fiancée, Herbsindia, Purité de Provence, Ôliv, LASHE Superfood, Candid, Caivil, Hercules, Black Chic, Code 10, Ingwe, X-Men, Thuan Phat and Isoplus.

Can Marico sustain its 9% domestic volume growth momentum into FY27 if rural consumption slows or commodity input costs such as copra prices rise significantly?

title: Beyond Parachute: Marico swaps coconut oil comfort for a premium growth playbook
content:
The company said it expects to sustain “high single-digit volume growth in the India business” while maintaining “mid-teen constant currency growth” in international markets.
At a consolidated level, it aims to deliver “double-digit revenue growth to cross ₹15,000 Cr. in FY27” and “high-teen EBITDA growth, subject to current macros.”
Also read: Marico ends FY26 strong, sees steady demand recovery ahead
The outlook marks a structural rebalancing of Marico’s portfolio. Premium Personal Care, Foods and digital-first brands are set to play a larger role in the revenue mix, with their India revenue share expected to rise from about 23% in FY26 to 27% in FY27 and 33% by FY30.
The company said sustained investments in these segments are driving a “structural shift in the revenue and profitability construct of the India business.”
Beyond the bottle
This transition comes even as Marico continues to lean on its core franchises for stability. The company said it expects “our core categories to chart a growth trajectory in line with medium-term aspirations,” supported by “healthy offtakes, penetration and market share gains across the key franchises.”
On the demand front, Marico flagged cautious optimism. “We are hopeful of a gradual improvement in consumption trends in the quarters ahead,” it said, pointing to benign inflation, policy stimulus and early signs of rural recovery.
However, it added that “retail inflation levels, the onset and progression of the monsoon season, and the trajectory of crude-sensitive and other key material costs” will remain critical variables.
Costs, copra and caution
Margins are likely to be shaped by a mixed input cost environment. The company highlighted “significant tailwinds in copra, with prices correcting ~35% from peak levels,” which should help offset pressure from crude-linked inputs that continue to show an inflationary bias due to geopolitical developments. Marico said it will rely on “pricing power of our market-leading franchises, continued cost management initiatives and strengthening supply chain capabilities” to sustain margin resilience.
International business remains a key growth lever. The company expects “strong momentum with mid-teen constant currency growth, driven by broad-based performance across markets,” alongside ongoing diversification. It noted that the revenue share of Bangladesh in the international portfolio is expected to decline further over time, while premium categories continue to expand their contribution.
Also read: Marico to acquire majority stake in protein supplement brand Cosmix valuing it at Rs 375 crore
Marico is also doubling down on distribution and channel strategy. It said growth will be supported by “transformative expansion in our direct reach footprint under Project SETU” and a sharper focus on urban and premium portfolios through organised retail and e-commerce.
Summing up its strategy, Managing Director and CEO Saugata Gupta said, “We remain committed to achieving competitive, top quartile outcomes in FY27, while steadfastly advancing towards our bold vision of surpassing ₹20,000 Crores in revenue by FY30.”
With a calibrated shift towards higher-margin segments and a watchful eye on input costs and demand recovery, Marico’s next phase of growth appears set to be driven less by its legacy coconut oil business and more by its expanding premium playbook.

title: Info Edge-backed Meritto's parent NoPaperForms Solutions files updated DRHP to raise Rs 375 crore in fresh capital via IPO
content:
Gurugram-headquartered education-focused technology platform NoPaperForms Solutions, which is backed by Info Edge (India), has filed its updated draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to raise capital through an IPO.
The AI-powered education SaaS provider has proposed to raise Rs 375 crore through the issuance of fresh equity shares, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) of 3.84 crore equity shares by investor Startup Investments (Holding).
Info Edge-owned Startup Investments (Holding) held 47.93 percent of the company’s pre-offer paid-up equity capital at the time of filing the updated DRHP on September 4.
The company is also considering raising up to Rs 75 crore through a pre-IPO placement, prior to the filing of the red herring prospectus. If the pre-IPO placement is undertaken, the amount raised will be deducted from the fresh issue component.
NoPaperForms Solutions, which develops software-as-a-service (SaaS), embedded payments and agentic AI products for the education industry, had approached the capital markets by filing its draft offer document through the confidential pre-filing route in November 2025. The document was subsequently approved by SEBI in March 2026.
The company claims to be India’s largest platform in the student enrolment and payments segment, operating through two flagship products, Meritto and Collexo, along with extended offerings such as the student engagement suite Pixi and Mio AI, which cater to various types of educational organisations.
Click Here To Read All IPO News
Promoted by Naveen Goyal, NoPaperForms Solutions will utilise Rs 96 crore of the net fresh issue proceeds for customer acquisition and retention, while Rs 148 crore will be used for technology development and cloud infrastructure. The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards general corporate purposes and funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions.
The company addresses student acquisition, enrolment, fee management and student engagement processes through its education platform. It derived 91 percent of its revenue from domestic operations in FY26, while its international business contributed around 9 percent.
Profit for the year ended March 2026 surged more than six-fold to Rs 11.9 crore from Rs 1.88 crore in the previous year, while revenue for the same period grew 25.2 percent to Rs 115.6 crore from Rs 92.3 crore. In the latest quarter ended June 2026, the company reported a profit of Rs 6 crore and revenue of Rs 44.7 crore.
IIFL Capital Services and SBI Capital Markets are the merchant bankers managing the NoPaperForms Solutions IPO.

title: MyGate raises ₹225 crore from Dharana Capital
content:
MyGate raises ₹225 crore from Dharana Capital
- MygateCompany
- DharanaInvestor
MyGate, the Indian community‑management platform, raised ₹225 crore (US$27.4 million) from Dharana Capital on July 5, 2026. The funding is earmarked for expanding advertising, smart‑lock hardware and other ancillary services, signaling a shift away from a pure subscription model.
MyGate has secured ₹225 crore (US$27.4 million) in growth‑stage funding from Dharana Capital on July 5, 2026, marking the latest infusion aimed at broadening its revenue mix beyond pure software subscriptions.
Deal Terms
The round was led solely by Dharana Capital; no other investors were disclosed and the specific valuation or equity percentage was not disclosed. MyGate said the capital will fund a multi‑pronged expansion that includes scaling its advertising business, rolling out smart‑lock hardware to resident doorways, and exploring additional services that leverage its resident data.
Strategic Rationale
According to co‑founder and CEO Abhishek Kumar, roughly 70 % of MyGate’s current revenue now comes from advertising, while smart‑lock sales contribute an additional 8‑9 %. “We don’t want to be a super app,” Kumar told *Mint*, adding that the company is moving “from the gate of the community to the door of the home.” The diversification is intended to offset the still‑evolving willingness of Indian consumers to pay for pure software, a challenge that has limited subscription scalability.
MyGate reported FY25 revenue of ₹186.7 crore, up from ₹109 crore a year earlier, and narrowed its net loss to ₹15.3 crore. The company’s growth comes as analysts estimate the addressable advertising opportunity in India’s gated‑community segment at nearly $800 million by FY31, with the total number of digitised communities expected to double to over 70,000.
The broader community‑tech landscape shows divergent paths. NoBrokerhood is cross‑selling home‑services and financial products, while Park+ is keeping advertising a modest supplement to its core parking and insurance business. Anacity, formerly ApnaComplex, has abandoned consumer advertising entirely to focus on enterprise real‑estate software. MyGate’s decision to stay within the residential‑community ecosystem—expanding into hardware and ads—positions it as a specialist rather than a super‑app, differentiating it from peers that are either broadening into services or retreating to enterprise solutions.
Why It Matters
For MyGate, the new capital accelerates a monetisation play that leans heavily on advertising and hardware, both of which generate higher gross margins than traditional subscription fees. By deepening its data‑driven ad stack, MyGate can improve net revenue retention and create a more defensible moat around its resident base, pressuring rivals like NoBrokerhood to prove the scalability of their service‑cross‑sell model. Park+, which has kept advertising a small fraction of revenue, may feel compelled to boost its own ad inventory to keep pace with MyGate’s growing ad share. Meanwhile, Anacity’s enterprise‑only focus underscores a bifurcation in the market: operators must choose between a consumer‑centric, multi‑revenue approach and a pure B2B software play.
Investors will watch how MyGate translates the fresh funding into sustainable expansion revenue. Success could validate a hybrid SaaS‑hardware model for other niche verticals, while a slowdown might reinforce the case for pure‑play enterprise platforms. The competitive dynamics will likely sharpen as each player refines its go‑to‑market motion within the rapidly expanding gated‑community ecosystem.
Key Points
- MyGate raised ₹225 crore (US$27.4 million) from Dharana Capital.
- Advertising now accounts for roughly 70 % of MyGate’s revenue.
- Smart‑lock hardware contributes 8‑9 % of revenue.
- FY25 revenue grew to ₹186.7 crore, up from ₹109 crore YoY, with net loss narrowing to ₹15.3 crore.
- India’s gated‑community advertising market is projected at $800 million by FY31.
Analysis
The ₹225 crore infusion gives MyGate a runway to deepen its hybrid SaaS‑hardware model at a time when vertical SaaS investors are rewarding companies that can demonstrate expansion revenue and high‑margin ancillary streams. While the round’s valuation was not disclosed, the size of the raise suggests a multiple in line with other high‑growth Indian SaaS firms that are trading between 10‑15 times FY25 revenue. The shift toward advertising and smart‑lock hardware aligns with a broader trend of community platforms leveraging resident data to unlock higher‑margin, recurring revenue beyond subscription churn. For operators, the deal underscores the importance of building a diversified revenue engine that can sustain growth as subscription willingness matures. For investors, MyGate’s trajectory highlights the appetite for capital in niche B2B SaaS businesses that can capture adjacent consumer spend, especially in a market where the addressable ad spend in gated communities is projected to reach $800 million by FY31. The funding also raises the bar for peers: firms that remain single‑product focused may need to accelerate their own diversification or risk being out‑scaled in gross margin and net revenue retention.

                                        The funding momentum continued through the second week of June, with investors backing ventures spanning artificial intelligence, deeptech, electric mobility and healthcare. 
While AI had a sweet spot among investors, capital also flowed into sectors such as precision oncology, paediatric healthcare and D2C brands, showing continued investor appetite for category-defining businesses.
ETEntrepreneur brings a roundup of key deals below.
Paediatric healthcare startup Hoola Health raises $5 million from Peak XV’s Surge, others
Paediatric healthcare startup Hoola Health, formerly known as BabyMD, has raised $5 million in a funding round led by Peak XV Partners’ seed investment platform Surge, as it looks to expand its network of child-focused clinics.
Existing investor W Health Ventures also participated in the round, along with multiple angel investors, including Ashish Gupta, Abhishek Goyal and Bijou Kurien.
The Bengaluru-headquartered startup, founded in 2024 by Deeksha Senguttuvan, offers paediatric consultations, vaccinations, diagnostics, developmental assessments and therapy services through neighbourhood clinics, supported by digital tools for parents.

Deeptech startup Ethereal Machines raises $28.5 million from Avataar Ventures, Peak XV, others
Precision manufacturing startup Ethereal Machines has raised $28.5 million in a round led by Avataar Ventures, with participation from Peak XV Partners and others. The Bengaluru-based deeptech startup was founded in 2014 by Kaushik Mudda and Navin Jain.
It designs and builds proprietary multi-axis CNC machines (automated tools that cut and carve) and operates a machining-as-a-service (MaaS) business supplying high-precision components to aerospace, defence, healthcare and semiconductor clients.
The company's flagship CNC machines, Aura and Nimbus, deliver sub-10-micron accuracy, a standard it claims is a first for Indian manufacturing.

title: MyGate Secures Rs 225 Cr From Dharana Capital To Accelerate Expansion
content:
Community management and security platform Mygate has raised Rs 225 crore (approximately USD 26 million) from Dharana Capital, marking its first major funding round in over three years, as per media reports.
As part of the transaction, Dharana Capital acquired a 12–14 per cent stake in the company through a combination of primary investment and secondary share purchases.
The fresh capital will be deployed to expand Mygate’s presence across gated residential communities, strengthen its integrated platform, and enhance product and technology capabilities. The company is targeting growth to 10 million homes in the coming years.
Founded by Abhishek Kumar, Shreyans Daga, Vijay Arisetty and Rohit Jindal, Mygate provides technology solutions for residential communities, enabling resident welfare associations (RWAs) and homeowners to manage visitor access, finances, amenities, communications, and other daily operations. The company also runs a consumer-brand engagement and advertising platform.
Mygate last raised capital in November 2022, securing a strategic investment of USD 12 million from Urban Company and Acko. Prior to that, it raised USD 56 million in a Series B round in 2019.
Dharana Capital is an India-focused growth-stage investment firm with portfolio companies including Urban Company, Vyapar, Zopper, Lentra, Itilite, Petpooja, Temple, LAT Aerospace and Beyond Appliances.

title: Mygate secures Rs 225 crore from Dharana Capital, eyes expansion to 10 million homes
content:
Indian community management and security platform Mygate has raised Rs 225 crore (around $26 million) from Dharana Capital, as it looks to expand its presence across gated communities and invest further in its technology platform.
The Bengaluru-based company plans to use the capital to grow from 5.7 million homes to 10 million homes, while strengthening its product and technology capabilities.
“We are looking to capitalise on our strength and expand Mygate rapidly from nearly 5.7 million homes to 10 million homes, by accelerating sign-ups across communities in India,” co-founder and CEO Abhishek Kumar said.
The company also plans to use part of the funding to support its expansion into international markets, including the Middle East.
As part of the transaction, Dharana Capital has acquired a 12% to 14% stake in Mygate through a mix of primary capital infusion and secondary share sales.
Founded in 2016 by Abhishek Kumar, Shreyans Daga and Vijay Arisetty, Mygate provides an app-based platform for residential communities to manage visitor access, security, payments, amenities, communications and other day-to-day operations.
Rohit Jindal, who joined Mygate in 2017 and served as chief business officer, was elevated to co-founder in June 2025. Vijay Arisetty, previously CEO of Mygate, became chairman of the company’s board in 2024 and later joined asset protection startup Aurm as founder and CEO.
Mygate earns revenue mainly through a software-as-a-service (SaaS) subscription model, under which residential communities and housing societies pay annual or multi-year fees for access to its tools. It also runs a brand engagement and advertising platform for consumer companies.
The company said it serves more than 27,000 residential communities and 5.7 million households across India.
Mygate reported operating revenue of Rs 173.5 crore in FY25, up from Rs 96.2 crore in FY24. Its net loss narrowed to Rs 15.4 crore from Rs 39.7 crore a year earlier.
The company said it would have been profitable in FY25 if not for Rs 22.5 crore in employee stock ownership plan and stock-based compensation expenses.
For FY26, Kumar said Mygate recorded revenue of Rs 232 crore and an EBITDA margin of 10% to 12%. The company did not disclose its net profit or loss for the year.
Mygate is targeting 37% year-on-year growth in operating revenue in FY27 and aims to be profit after tax positive.
The latest investment is Mygate’s first major funding round in more than three years. The company has previously raised more than $80 million from investors including Tiger Global, Tencent, Prime Venture Partners, Acko and Urban Company.
Dharana Capital is an India-focused growth-stage investment firm. Its portfolio includes Urban Company, Vyapar, Zopper, Lentra, Itilite, Petpooja, Temple, LAT Aerospace and Beyond Appliances.

title: Mygate closes Rs 225 crore deal with Dharana Capital
content:
Housing society management platform Mygate has closed a Rs 225 crore deal with Dharana Capital, which has backed the likes of Urban Company and Deepinder Goyal-backed Temple.
Of this, about Rs 100 crore is primary capital, while the remaining Rs 125 crore is a secondary transaction in which early investors, including Prime Venture Partners, and some senior employees sold shares, according to people aware of the matter.
The investment values the Bengaluru-based startup at around Rs 2,000-2,200 crore, sources said, compared to its last valuation of around Rs 1,600-1,700 crore in 2023. MyGate has so far raised about $84 million from investors like Tiger Global, Prime Venture Partners, and Tencent.
"We will continue to expand our gated community offerings across India and invest deeply in technology because, at heart, we are a tech company," Mygate cofounder and CEO Abhishek Kumar told ET.
He added that despite serving affluent gated communities, customers remain reluctant to pay for software. "Nearly 70% of our revenue comes from advertising, around 25% from our core software offering, and about 5% from the smart devices vertical," he said.
Founded in 2016 by Kumar, Vijay Arisetty, and Shreyans Daga, Mygate began as a visitor management platform and has since evolved into a broader operating system for gated communities. It now serves more than 27,000 residential complexes and 5.7 million homes across India.
"We expect the contribution from our software business to increase as we scale to 10 million homes. Larger housing societies are increasingly being built across the country, which is a tailwind for us. We are also taking MyGate's services outside India and testing operations in the Middle East," Kumar said.
The platform offers software for gate and security management, finance and accounting, amenity booking, internal communications, and other housing society operations. In September 2024, it expanded into hardware with the launch of Mygate Locks, a range of smart door locks.
The company underwent a leadership transition in 2024, with Kumar taking over as chief executive after cofounder Vijay Arisetty stepped down from the role. Arisetty continues as chairman of Mygate's board and has since founded a fintech, Aurm, where he’s the CEO.
Mygate recorded revenues of around Rs 230 crore in FY26, a 23% increase from the previous year. In FY25, the company reported revenues of Rs 186.7 crore, up from Rs 109 crore a year earlier, while narrowing its net loss to Rs 15.3 crore from Rs 39.7 crore in FY24.
Commenting on the investment, Vamsi Duvvuri, founder and managing partner at Dharana Capital, said, "We believe urban India's shift towards gated communities is an irreversible trend, and Mygate provides an essential platform to power these ecosystems."

title: Dharana Capital invests Rs 225 crore in Mygate
content:
Dharana Capital invests Rs 225 crore in Mygate
Mygate to deploy funds towards expanding its gated community footprint and strengthening its integrated platform
Published: Jun 10, 2026 11:40 AM | 2 min read
- Dharana Capital has invested Rs 225 crore in Mygate, a leading technology platform for residential community management in India.
- Mygate serves over 27,000 residential communities and 5.7 million homes, offering solutions for gate management, finance, amenities, and internal communications.
- The investment aims to support Mygate's growth, with plans to expand its reach to 10 million homes and enhance its product and technology capabilities.
- Both Dharana Capital and Mygate's leadership emphasized the importance of Mygate's role in urban India's shift towards gated communities and its established market leadership.
Dharana Capital has announced an investment of Rs 225 Cr in Mygate, India’s leading technology platform for residential community management. Combining a full-stack toolkit for housing society RWAs (Resident Welfare Associations) and a resident engagement app, Mygate’s solutions are trusted by over 27,000 residential communities and 5.7 million homes.
Mygate’s platform has been the lifeline for RWAs that depend on its comprehensive suite of solutions, including management of gate & security, finance & accounting, amenities, internal communications, and much more. The platform also features a built-in brand engagement and advertising layer offering brands a powerful channel to engage with communities at scale.
Commenting on the development, Vamsi Duvvuri, Founder and Managing Partner, Dharana Capital, said: “Mygate is a household brand in the community management category and, through the team’s disciplined execution, has established clear market leadership. We believe that urban India’s move towards gated communities is an irreversible trend and Mygate provides an essential platform to power these ecosystems. We look forward to working closely with the founders to support the company’s next phase of growth.”
Abhishek Kumar, Co-founder and CEO, Mygate, added: “We are excited to have Dharana Capital join us in our growth journey. Dharana’s deep engagement with portfolio companies makes them a strong partner in our efforts to enhance the breadth and depth of our platform. Over the last three years, Mygate has delivered more than 3x revenue growth while achieving profitability and reinforcing its market leadership position. Our unwavering focus on solving real problems for gated communities at scale has been central to this journey. We will use the fresh capital to accelerate Mygate’s expansion towards 10 million homes, deepen our product and technology capabilities, and build a more intelligent, integrated operating system for residential communities.”

title: Dharana Capital buys 12-14% stake worth  ₹225 crore in Mygate
content:
MUMBAI: Dharana Capital has acquired a 12-14% stake in residential community management platform Mygate for about ₹225 crore, backing the startup's plans to expand its presence across India and broaden its product offerings, a top executive said.
The transaction values Mygate between ₹2,100 crore and ₹2,300 crore and comprises a mix of primary capital and secondary share sales by some early investors seeking partial exits, co-founder and chief executive Abhishek Kumar told Mint in an interview.
“We believe that urban India’s move towards gated communities is an irreversible trend and Mygate provides an essential platform to power these ecosystems,” Dharana’s founder and managing partner Vamsi Duvvuri said.
The fresh capital will be used to accelerate Mygate's expansion into newer markets. "We are running experiments and have taken our products to the Middle East, where we are currently running pilots. We are also looking to enter additional payment solutions for households," Kumar said.
Founded in 2016 by Kumar, Vijay Arisetty and Shreyans Daga, Mygate operates a technology platform aimed at improving life within gated communities. The company serves more than 27,000 residential communities and over 5.7 million households, offering products spanning security, finance and accounting, and resident engagement.
To date, the company has raised more than $80 million from investors including Tiger Global Management, Tencent Holdings and Prime Venture Partners, as well as strategic investors such as Acko and Urban Company. According to Tracxn, Mygate was last valued at about ₹1,670 crore in April 2023.
Mygate seeks to enable seamless interactions among residents, management committees and service providers while improving transparency and operational efficiency. Over time, the platform has evolved from a visitor management solution into a broader ecosystem that includes local services discovery, maintenance payments and a marketplace for used goods.
“Over the last four years, we have taken a conscious call to growth sustainably and build a profitable enterprise after spending the initial few years in the distribution phase of the company and establishing product market fit,” Kumar said. He added that the company has grown about 34-35% in operating revenue through FY26 and has a strong trajectory to profitability.
In FY25, Mygate reported an 80% increase in operating revenue to ₹173.5 crore from ₹96.2 crore a year earlier, while narrowing its net loss to ₹15.4 crore from ₹39.7 crore in FY24.
Dharana Capital is an India-focused growth-stage technology and consumer investment firm. Its portfolio includes Urban Company, LAT Aerospace, Vyapar, Temple, Zopper, Lentra, Itilite, Petpooja and Beyond Appliances. The firm is backed by leading US university endowments and other non-profit institutions.

Mygate had last raised Rs 100 crore in November 2022. The startup has evolved from a visitor management solution into an ecosystem that encompasses all aspects of the gated community experience, such as local service discovery, maintenance payments, and a marketplace for used goods.
Vamsi Duvvuri, Founder and Managing Partner, Dharana Capital, said, “We believe that urban India’s move towards gated communities is an irreversible trend and Mygate provides an essential platform to power these ecosystems."
Dharana Capital is an India-focused growth-stage investment firm focused on technology and consumer companies. It is backed by top US University endowments and other non-profit institutions. Its portfolio of companies includes Urban Company, LAT Aerospace, Vyapar, Temple, Zopper, Lentra, Itilite, Petpooja, and Beyond Appliances.

title: Purple Style Labs Ltd (NSE:PERNIASPOP): Why Did Losses Remain Elevated Despite Higher Luxury Fashion Sales?
content:
Highlights
- Consolidated revenue increased approximately 13% year on year during Q1 FY27.
- Net loss narrowed to INR 88.13 crore but remained substantial.
- Finance costs and depreciation significantly influenced reported earnings.
- The company listed on NSE and BSE on September 7, 2026.
- Luxury experience centres and international operations remain important business developments.
Purple Style Labs Reports Higher Sales Amid Continued Losses
Purple Style Labs Ltd (NSE:PERNIASPOP) operates a luxury fashion retail business offering designer apparel, accessories, jewellery and lifestyle products.
Its retail portfolio includes Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, which connects customers with Indian designer labels through online and physical channels.
The company's first quarterly results following its September 2026 listing showed higher revenue but continuing losses.
The financial position reflects substantial expenditure associated with retail infrastructure, employees and financing.
What Do the Q1 FY27 Results Reveal?
Purple Style Labs reported consolidated revenue from operations of INR 119.44 crore during Q1 FY27.
The supplied comparative research reports INR 105.7 crore in Q1 FY26, indicating approximately 13% growth.
Consolidated total income reached INR 121.90 crore.
However, total expenses amounted to INR 202.05 crore.
The company reported a net loss of INR 88.13 crore, compared with approximately INR 100.3 crore in the corresponding quarter.
Although the loss narrowed, expenditure remained considerably above income.
Why Did Operating Expenses Remain Elevated?
The official financial filing reported employee benefit expenses of INR 25.19 crore during Q1 FY27.
Finance costs reached INR 33.99 crore, while depreciation and amortisation amounted to INR 34.84 crore.
Other operating expenses stood at INR 31.30 crore.
These expenditure categories reflect the financial requirements associated with the company's business structure.
The combined financing and depreciation costs were particularly significant relative to quarterly revenue.
Maintaining store productivity and controlling operating expenditure therefore remain important considerations.
What Was the Exceptional Expense?
Purple Style Labs recognised an exceptional charge of INR 7.98 crore during Q1 FY27.
The company's official financial statement identifies this as employee compensation expenditure arising from stock-option grants.
Before the exceptional item, the consolidated loss was INR 80.15 crore.
After recognising the charge, the loss increased to INR 88.13 crore.
This distinction is important because the exceptional expense contributed to the reported loss.
Nevertheless, the company remained loss-making before the adjustment.
Luxury Retail and Customer Spending
Purple Style Labs serves customers purchasing designer clothing and accessories for weddings, celebrations and other occasions.
Its business includes online sales and physical experience centres.
The supplied investor-presentation summary reports gross merchandise value of approximately INR 193 crore during Q1 FY27, compared with INR 133 crore a year earlier.
Average order value reportedly increased to INR 86,000 from INR 66,000.
These figures indicate higher marketplace activity and larger average transactions.
However, gross merchandise value is different from recognised revenue.
Experience Centres and Overseas Expansion
The company has expanded its retail presence through luxury experience centres.
The supplied research identifies new locations in Mumbai and New York becoming operational during the June 2026 quarter.
Its official consolidated financial filing includes subsidiaries incorporated in India, the United Kingdom and the United States.
International expansion may increase access to overseas customers.
However, additional locations introduce rental, staffing, marketing and operational expenses.
Their contribution to profitability depends on sales productivity and operating efficiency.
What Changed After the September Listing?
Purple Style Labs completed an initial public offering consisting entirely of a fresh equity issue.
The issue raised INR 680 crore, and shares were listed on September 7, 2026.
The company's September financial filing states that utilisation of IPO proceeds would be reported in the subsequent reporting period.
Accordingly, the entire amount raised should not be treated as already deployed.
The company's future disclosures will provide more information about capital allocation and expenditure.
What Challenges Could Influence Performance?
Purple Style Labs operates in a discretionary luxury market influenced by customer preferences and occasion-based purchases.
Experience centres require considerable fixed expenditure.
Finance costs, depreciation and employee expenses can continue affecting profitability even when revenue increases.
International operations also introduce additional administrative requirements.
The company must balance expansion with cash requirements, operating efficiency and customer demand.
Key Insights
Purple Style Labs Ltd (NSE:PERNIASPOP) reported higher revenue and a narrower consolidated loss during Q1 FY27.
However, expenses substantially exceeded income, with financing and depreciation contributing significantly.
The company's September listing and expanding retail presence marked important developments.
Store productivity, cash requirements, operating expenses and the utilisation of IPO proceeds remain relevant considerations.
FAQs
Q: What is the NSE ticker of Purple Style Labs Ltd?
A: Its official NSE trading symbol is NSE:PERNIASPOP.
Q: What was the company's revenue in Q1 FY27?
A: Consolidated revenue from operations reached INR 119.44 crore.
Q: Did Purple Style Labs report a profit?
A: No. It reported a consolidated net loss of INR 88.13 crore.
Q: When did the company list on NSE?
A: Its shares were listed on September 7, 2026.
Q: What are its principal business challenges?
A: High operating expenses, financing costs, retail infrastructure requirements and the profitability of new locations remain important considerations.

title: ESDS, Lumino, Purple Style Labs: 18 IPO stocks facing anchor lock-in expiry in October - Check full list
content:
The October IPO calendar is set to bring another important event for investors tracking recently listed stocks, with shares allotted to anchor investors in 18 companies becoming eligible for trading during the month. According to a fortnightly review by PL Research, these lock-in expiries cover 14 companies under the 30-day period and four companies under the 90-day period between October 5 and October 16, 2026. Anchor investors typically receive shares before an IPO opens to the broader public, but those shares remain locked for a specified period. Once the lock-in expires, the shares become eligible for trading. This does not necessarily mean that investors will sell the shares, but the additional tradable supply can become an important factor for market participants, particularly when a stock has delivered strong gains since listing. As per the report, among the 14 companies approaching their 30-day lock-in expiry, Purple Style Labs and Manipal Payment & Identity Solutions have the highest proportion of shares becoming eligible for trading, at around 22% of their respective total shares. Rays of Belief follows with around 20%. Lumino Industries, ESDS Software Solution, Priority Jewels, Deepa Jewellers, Glass Wall Systems, Prasol Chemicals, Kanohar Electricals, Rentomojo, Asset Reconstruction Co. (India) and Steamhouse India each have approximately 15% of their total shares becoming eligible for trading. Pranav Constructions has the lowest proportion among this group at around 12%. The individual lock-in data shows that Purple Style Labs has 26,60,869 shares, or 22%, becoming eligible on the 30-day expiry, while Manipal Payment & Identity Solutions has 53,42,916 shares, also representing 22%. Rays of Belief has 10,46,095 shares, or 20%, becoming eligible. For investors, the scale of the potential supply is particularly relevant when compared with the company's total outstanding shares and recent price performance. The report notes that most of the upcoming 30-day expiries involve around 15% of total shares. “The proportion of shares becoming eligible for trading ranges from approximately 12% to 22% of the respective companies’ total shares, with most companies seeing around 15% of total shares come out of lock-in,” PL Research said. Several of these stocks have already delivered substantial gains since their IPOs. ESDS Software Solution was trading around 234% above its issue price, while Glass Wall Systems was up 51%, Priority Jewels 47%, Steamhouse India 35%, Kanohar Electricals 34% and Rentomojo 27%. Manipal Payment & Identity Solutions and Prasol Chemicals were both around 21% above their issue prices, while Lumino Industries was up 21%. Deepa Jewellers was 11% higher and Asset Reconstruction Co. (India) was up 3%. “Stock performance across the upcoming 30-day unlocks remains largely positive, with 11 of the 14 companies currently trading above their IPO issue price. In contrast, Pranav Constructions was trading 20% below its issue price, Purple Style Labs was down 7% and Rays of Belief was down 5% from their respective IPO issue prices. The four companies approaching their 90-day anchor lock-in expiry are Knack Packaging, Kusumgar, Laser Power & Infra and SBI Funds Management. Around 14–15% of total shares in each company will become eligible for trading. Kusumgar was trading around 43% above its issue price, followed by Laser Power & Infra at 23% and Knack Packaging at 6%. Knack Packaging has 38,60,294 shares, or 15%, scheduled to unlock on October 5. The upcoming expiries therefore create an important supply event across a diverse set of recently listed companies. While the unlocking of anchor shares does not automatically indicate selling, investors may track trading volumes, price movements and the behaviour of anchor shareholders around the respective expiry dates. A shrinking loss combined with double-digit revenue growth is generally read as a sign of improving unit economics, since it suggests the company is generating more revenue per rupee of loss than it was a year ago. title: Purple Style Labs In Focus After Approving $7 Million Investment In US Subsidiary
content:
The firm is an omnichannel platform in luxury fashion that runs under the name Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop. The firm sells luxury clothing items, jewelry, and other fashion-related products via digital platforms and experience centers.
The shares of Purple Style are currently trading at Rs. 539.55, up by 1.16%. The company has a market capitalization of Rs. 4,315.69 crore. The stock’s 52 week high is Rs. 588.90 and its 52 week low is Rs. 511.50. In the past 6 months the stok has delivered a return of -5.19%.
What's The News
Purple Style Labs’ Board of Directors, through their meeting on September 21, 2026, has approved the amount of $7 million as an investment in its wholly-owned subsidiary Purple Style Labs USA, Inc. This will be done through the acquisition of 7 million Class B Common Stock of PSL USA at a par value of $1 each. As a result, Purple Style Labs will still maintain 100% ownership of the common stock of its US subsidiary.
The investment is proposed to be mainly sourced from the net proceeds of the company's recent initial public offering (IPO), where up to approximately Rs. 53 crore can be set aside for this investment. The money shall be utilized by PSL USA for corporate purposes as stated in the company's IPO offer document.
Investment Details
Purple Style Labs Ltd has approved an investment of approximately Rs. 62.5 crore in its wholly owned subsidiary, Purple Style Labs USA, Inc. The investment will involve the acquisition of 70 lakh Class B Common Stock shares at a par value of approximately Rs. 89 per share.
The investment will be funded through the company’s IPO proceeds, and Purple Style Labs will continue to hold 100% ownership in the US subsidiary following the investment. The transaction is classified as a related-party transaction and is subject to approval from the authorised dealer bank under FEMA.
The investment is expected to be completed within 30 days of receiving the required regulatory approval.
Focus on US Luxury Retail
PSL USA was formed in Delaware on April 16, 2025, and functions in the luxury retail industry in the USA. The subsidiary runs a physical experience studio in New York City under the Pernia's Pop-Up Studio brand, where it deals with various product segments, such as women’s wear, men’s wear, jewelry, accessories, and kidswear.
PSL USA has turnover of around Rs. 1.158 crore for the period of April 16, 2025, to March 31, 2026. Since the company was set up in FY26, it does not have any historical data of turnover for other previous periods.
Related-Party Transaction
As the entity PSL USA is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Purple Style Labs, the proposed transaction would be treated as a related party transaction under Section 2(76) of the Companies Act, 2013.
The Company has revealed that the transaction is to be done at arm's length and is consistent with the objects mentioned in the prospectus of the IPO. Abhishek Agarwal is serving as Whole-time Director & CEO of Purple Style Labs and President, Secretary and Treasurer of PSL USA.
IPO Proceeds Deployment
The latest investment comes shortly after Purple Style Labs raised Rs. 680 crore through its IPO, which comprised entirely of a fresh issue.
The company's IPO proceeds were earmarked for purposes including investment in its wholly owned Indian subsidiary PSL Retail, expenditure towards lease liabilities of experience centres and back-end offices, sales and marketing expenses and general corporate purposes. The latest Rs. 62.5 crore investment in PSL USA therefore represents another deployment of capital following the company's recent listing.
Investor Perspective
The Rs. 62.5 crore investment in PSL USA marks an expansion of Purple Style Labs' capital commitment to its international luxury retail operations. The investment will provide additional capital to the US subsidiary while Purple Style Labs retains full ownership of the business.
For investors, the key factors to track will include regulatory approval and completion of the transaction, revenue generation from the New York experience centre, utilisation of IPO proceeds and the performance of the company's international operations.
The relatively small Rs. 1.158 crore FY26 turnover reported by PSL USA also means that the contribution of the US business to the consolidated operations will be an important metric to monitor as the company scales its international presence.

title: Purple Style Labs Approves $7 Million US Subsidiary Investment From IPO Proceeds
content:
Purple Style Labs Approves $7 Million US Subsidiary Investment From IPO Proceeds
Purple Style Labs will deploy up to ₹53 crore ($7 million) of its recent ₹680 crore IPO proceeds to fund retail expansion in the US. The board has approved acquiring 7 million Class B shares of PSL USA, which runs the Pernia's Pop-Up Shop experience centre in New York. The related-party transaction requires FEMA clearance and is targeted for completion within 30 days of approval.
Market snapshot: Purple Style Labs Limited has approved a cash investment of $7 million in its wholly owned US subsidiary, Purple Style Labs USA, Inc. (PSL USA), to acquire 7 million Class B Common Stock shares at $1 par value. Sourced from up to ₹53 crore of its recent IPO proceeds, the transaction will support the Delaware-incorporated unit's retail business in the United States, including its New York City experience centre.
Data Snapshot
- US Subsidiary Cash Investment
- IPO Proceeds Sourced
- Parent Company Total IPO Size
- US Subsidiary FY26 Turnover
What's Changed
- Domestic vs International Subsidiary Funding: Following a massive ₹420 crore allocation into its domestic unit (PSL Retail) on September 15, 2026, the company has pivoted its capital distribution to international markets with a $7 million allocation for its Delaware-incorporated unit on September 21, 2026.
Key Takeaways
- The $7 million capital injection will reinforce PSL USA's physical luxury retail hub in New York City, targeting high-margin global luxury clientele.
- The transaction acquires 7 million Class B shares at $1 par value, structured as an arm's length related-party deal under Section 2(76) of the Companies Act, 2013.
- Utilizing up to ₹53 crore of net IPO proceeds aligns strictly with the international footprint expansion goals disclosed in the company's prospectus.
- Outbound transfer remains subject to regulatory clearance from an Authorized Dealer bank under FEMA rules.
SAHI Perspective
While the $7 million (₹53 crore) capital injection into PSL USA aligns with the company's global expansion ambitions, it comes against a backdrop of tight operational performance. Purple Style Labs listed at a 6.96% discount on NSE at ₹535.00 on September 7, 2026, reflecting investor concern over its financial profile. For FY26, consolidated losses widened ≈51.5% YoY (derived: -₹285.40 crore vs -₹188.38 crore in FY25), driven by heavy lease liabilities and interest costs. The US subsidiary itself generated a modest turnover of ₹1.16 crore for the period ending March 31, 2026. Deploying critical IPO funds to support a highly capital-intensive global brick-and-mortar footprint in New York may exacerbate operational cash burn unless international revenues scale rapidly.
Market Implications
The decision highlights the company's reliance on physical experience centres to drive brand equity and premium retail sales. However, with heavy front-loaded costs and widening losses at the parent level, the market may view the high capital allocation to loss-making subsidiaries with skepticism. In the medium term, the stock price (currently trading near ₹550) is likely to remain under pressure until there is clear evidence of a path to profitability and improved operational leverage.
Trading Signals
Market Bias: Bearish
Despite the expansionary signal of the $7 million US investment, the parent company faces widening net losses (₹285.40 crore in FY26) and a weak stock market debut at a 6.96% discount. Continued capital deployment into physical hubs may keep near-term operational cash flows negative.
Underweight: Speciality Retail
Trigger Factors:
- FEMA / AD Bank approval timeline for the $7 million transaction
- Q1 FY27 consolidated earnings release showing path to loss reduction
- Footfall and sales velocity data from the New York experience centre
Time Horizon: Near-term (0-3 months)
Industry Context
The Indian luxury fashion market has seen structural shifts with rising disposable incomes, pushing premium platforms to scale globally. However, international luxury retailing is highly competitive and capital-heavy. Multi-brand luxury players like Purple Style Labs face high customer acquisition costs and substantial rent overheads in prime global retail hubs like New York and London. Operating under a 15% SKU service-fee arrangement with its subsidiaries, the parent company is highly dependent on the retail turnaround of these physical experience centres.
Key Risks to Watch
- Capital-heavy physical retail centers in high-rent zones like New York City could drain IPO proceeds without delivering commensurate margin improvements.
- Any delay or denial of FEMA approval from the Authorized Dealer bank may stall the transaction beyond the 30-day target timeline.
- Sourcing funds in INR (₹53 crore) for investment in USD ($7 million) exposes the company to exchange rate fluctuations.
- Widening consolidated losses (reaching -₹285.40 crore in FY26) limit the company's financial flexibility.
Recent Developments
On September 15, 2026, Purple Style Labs approved a major investment of ₹420 crore in its domestic wholly owned subsidiary, PSL Retail, through a rights issue funded by the IPO proceeds to manage lease obligations. The company listed on BSE and NSE on September 7, 2026, at ₹539.00 and ₹535.00 respectively, a discount of up to 6.96% against its IPO issue price of ₹575.00.
Closing Insight
Purple Style Labs is aggressively executing its IPO-stated capital deployment strategy. However, expanding physical presence in high-cost global capitals while struggling with escalating domestic losses presents a high-risk, high-reward path that public market investors will monitor with extreme caution.

title: Purple Style Labs Board Approves ₹420 Cr Investment in Wholly Owned Subsidiary PSL Retail
content:
Decision of Board of Directors of Purple Style Labs dated September 15, 2026 – The Board of Directors of Purple Style Labs have decided to invest Rs. 420 crores in their wholly owned subsidiary company PSL Retail Private Limited by acquiring equity shares through rights issue.
The investment is being made in line with the objects of Purple Style Labs’ recent IPO. The company plans to utilise a portion of the net proceeds from its fresh equity issue for this investment.
Investment Details
The Rs. 420 crore investment will be made through a rights issue in PSL Retail. The transaction involves the acquisition of 42 crore equity shares at Rs. 10 per share, according to the reported transaction details. The investment is expected to be completed between September 19 and September 25, 2026.

PSL Retail Business

The investment therefore represents a capital infusion into the company's core retail business. The funds can help PSL Retail meet its lease-related obligations while supporting the company's expanding physical retail network.
IPO Proceeds to Support Retail Expansion
Purple Style Labs recently raised Rs. 680 crore through its IPO, which comprised entirely of a fresh issue of equity shares. The company had disclosed that a significant portion of the IPO proceeds would be used for investment in PSL Retail towards lease liabilities of experience centres and back-end offices.
Financial performance
Looking at the financial performance of Purple Style Labs Limited, the company’s consolidated revenue from operations increased by around 13.86 percent YoY, from Rs. 489.91 crore in FY25 to Rs. 557.84 crore in FY26.
In FY26, Purple Style Labs reported a consolidated net loss of Rs. 285 crore, compared with a net loss of Rs. 188 crore in FY25, indicating a significant widening of losses during the year. The company’s EPS stood at negative Rs. 41.83 in FY26, compared with negative EPS of around Rs. 44,959.43 in FY25.
Investor Perspective
The Rs. 420 crore investment strengthens the capital base of PSL Retail, the subsidiary operating Purple Style Labs' core luxury retail business. The deployment of IPO proceeds towards lease liabilities and corporate requirements could support the company's ongoing expansion of its physical retail network.
For investors, the key factors to monitor will be growth in retail revenue, store-level performance, operating margins, cash generation and the company's ability to manage lease and other fixed costs. The latest transaction itself is a capital allocation move, so its eventual impact on financial performance will depend on how effectively the funds support the expansion and operations of PSL Retail.
Company Overview
Purple Style Labs Limited is a luxury fashion and lifestyle company operating Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, an omnichannel platform offering designer and premium fashion products. The company combines its online presence with physical experience centres across key domestic and international markets.
The company focuses on luxury apparel, accessories and designer fashion, working with established and emerging designers. Its retail subsidiary, PSL Retail Private Limited, operates a significant part of the Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop business and supports the company’s expansion in the luxury retail segment.

title: Purple Style Labs Makes Weak Debut, Lists Nearly 7% Below IPO Price
content:
Purple Style Labs Makes Weak Debut, Lists Nearly 7% Below IPO Price
Shares of Purple Style Labs, the parent company of luxury fashion platform Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, made a weak debut on Dalal Street on Monday, 07 September despite the company’s public issue receiving overall subscription.
The stock opened at Rs 535 on the NSE, a 6.96 per cent discount to its issue price of Rs 575 per share. On the BSE, it debuted at Rs 539, down 6.26 per cent from the issue price. The stock was trading at a 2 per cent discount in the grey market ahead of listing.
The Rs 680-crore IPO was subscribed 1.29 times, with investors bidding for around 88.66 lakh shares against 68.49 lakh shares on offer. Retail investors led demand with 1.58 times subscription, followed by qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) at 1.43 times. The non-institutional investor (NII) portion was undersubscribed at 84 per cent.
The issue, which was open from August 31 to September 2, comprised entirely a fresh issue of 1.18 crore equity shares, with no offer-for-sale component. The price band was fixed at Rs 546-575 per share.
Ahead of the IPO, Purple Style Labs raised Rs 306 crore from anchor investors on August 28. It allotted 53.21 lakh shares at Rs 575 apiece to 10 anchor investors, including Morgan Stanley Asia, BofA Securities Europe, Integrated Core Strategies, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Jupiter India Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance Company, ITI Mutual Fund and Singularity Equity Fund I.
A substantial portion of the fresh issue proceeds will be deployed towards the company’s subsidiary, PSL Retail. According to the IPO documents, the funds will be used to meet lease liabilities for Experience Centers and back-end offices in India, along with sales and marketing expenses and general corporate purposes.
Purple Style Labs operates Pernia’s Pop-Up Shop, a multi-brand luxury fashion platform offering designer apparel, jewellery and accessories across its digital platform and physical Experience Centers.
The company currently operates 14 Experience Centers, including 12 in metropolitan cities, while also reaching customers through online channels, events and exhibitions.
The company reported revenue from operations of around Rs 557.8 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 489.9 crore in FY25.
However, profitability remained under pressure. Purple Style Labs’ net loss widened to around Rs 285.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 188.3 crore in the previous financial year.

title: Purple Style Labs: Fewer customers, bigger losses
content:
Anand Kumar/AI-Generated Image
हिंदी में भी पढ़ें
Summary: A year before asking the public to pay Rs 575 a share, the founder quietly sold a chunk of his own stock for less. The celebrity names on the shareholder list took all the attention on listing day. The detail worth sitting with is a few pages deeper in the prospectus, and it reframes the whole offer.
Purple Style Labs, the owner of the luxury fashion platform Pernia's Pop-Up Shop, listed on September 7, 2026, at Rs 535, nearly 7 per cent below its Rs 575 issue price. The Rs 680 crore issue was subscribed only 1.36 times overall. For an investor hunting exceptional businesses at fair prices, the weak debut matters less than what sits underneath it.
What Pernia's actually sells
Abhishek Agarwal founded Purple Style Labs in 2015 and bought the Pernia's Pop-Up Shop website for about Rs 12 crore in 2018. He turned it into a chain of large "experience centres" in India, London and New York, selling wedding and occasion wear, jewellery and accessories from more than a thousand independent designers. A customer can shop online or walk into a store, and the company then sources the item on back-order, on consignment, or from its own limited stock, which keeps the inventory bill lower than a conventional multi-brand retailer.
The company frames itself as a platform connecting designers with affluent shoppers. But a platform should get stronger as it grows, and this one is not. Active designer brands on the site have fallen every year, from 1,910 in FY24 to 1,312 in FY25 to 1,109 in FY26. The top ten designers now supply nearly a third of gross sales, up from about a fifth two years ago, a network meant to widen with scale instead narrowing around fewer big names. There is no obvious switching cost stopping a shopper from buying straight from a designer's own boutique, and no clear cost advantage over a rival aggregator.
Who is backing it, and who is running it
The shareholder list reads like a red-carpet guest list: Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Madhuri Dixit and Sachin Tendulkar. It makes for good headlines but should do no work in an investment case. The real capital came from five funding rounds between 2018 and 2023 and a Rs 306 crore anchor book at the IPO.
Agarwal, an IIT Bombay engineer, has run the company for a decade. He held 26.1 per cent of it before the IPO, a stake now diluted to 22.3 per cent. But he privately sold about Rs 45 crore of his own shares in August 2025 at Rs 500 apiece, below even the IPO's Rs 546 floor. Asking new shareholders to pay more than he himself accepted a year earlier is not disqualifying by itself, but it is not the mark of an owner we would back without reservations. A permanent employee attrition rate of 46 per cent in FY26, in a business built around personal styling, adds to that unease.
The numbers behind the ‘premiumisation’ story
This was once a much faster business. Revenue grew from about Rs 45 crore in FY20 to over Rs 500 crore in FY24, a pace that has since stalled to about 5 per cent a year. Management's defence is that it deliberately dropped lower-value designers and products to chase richer customers, and the average order value backs this up, rising from Rs 45,513 to Rs 75,505 in two years, with Indian stores earning more than double the ticket size of the website.
But the outcome has not followed the intent. Losses have widened every single year rather than narrowing as the business matured. Gross margin slipped from about 42 per cent to 38 per cent, and the EBITDA margin nearly halved even as sales grew, because employee costs rose faster than revenue. Working capital tied up in the business roughly doubled over the same period, as new stores were stocked and staffed ahead of the sales they were meant to generate.
What it is worth
At the issue price, the company was valued near Rs 4,600 crore, about eight times FY26 revenue, with losses instead of a P/E to anchor the multiple, and no comparable listed business in India to check that multiple against, a fact the company itself admits in its prospectus. Work backwards instead: even a generous eventual 10 per cent net margin and a 30 times P/E would require revenue near Rs 1,530 crore, close to three times today's level, alongside a full swing from heavy losses into consistent profit. That is not a price on the business Purple Style Labs is today. It is a price on the business it might become.
The risks, honestly
Set the accounting loss aside and the structural risks still stack up. Of the Rs 680 crore raised, Rs 371 crore goes to settling lease liabilities on stores already built, and Rs 139 crore to marketing, leaving little for anything genuinely new. Four large stores opened in FY26 alone and still need to prove they can earn their keep. The top 10,000 customers, barely 15 per cent of the base, already generate more than half of all sales, so the business depends on a narrow, wealthy cohort staying loyal.
Our verdict
The business and management pillars fail before valuation even enters the conversation. The designer network is shrinking rather than widening, the founder sold personal stock below the price he now asks the public to pay, and profits have moved further away every year, not closer. A newly listed, loss-making retailer priced for a transformation that has not yet begun is exactly the kind of story we would ask readers to sit out.
